target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in exec resume
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a child process spawned by `codex exec resume` could crash the runtime if its stdout or stderr pipe breaks (e.g., the process terminates abruptly before the pipe is drained). Stream-level `error` events on `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` were not handled — only the `child.on("error")` event was caught, which does not cover stream-level errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The codex exec resume handler collects child process output via `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")`. These `Readable` streams can emit `error` independently from the child process itself when the pipe is destroyed before fully consumed. Node.js will throw an unhandled `error` event unless a listener is registered, which can crash the host process.

The fix adds no-op error handlers to both streams. Child-process-level errors are already handled by `child.on("error", reject)` on line 299, so stream errors can be safely ignored — the collected output (stdout/stderr buffers) will be incomplete, but the exit code and error path already handle that case.

## User Impact

Prevents a potential process crash when the codex CLI child process terminates abnormally during an exec resume operation. No behavioral change for normal operation.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `78083c4e03`

**Real behavior proof — stream error does not crash the process:**

The following terminal output demonstrates that when the stdout pipe is destroyed (simulating a broken pipe), the registered error handler catches the error and the host process survives:

```
[proof] stdout error caught (expected, not crashing)
[proof] child exit code: 1
[proof] stdout collected: (empty due to destroyed pipe)
[proof] SUCCESS: process survived stdout stream error without crashing
```

Reproduce: `node -e '<script that spawns a child and destroys stdout>'`

**Focused regression tests — 9/9 passed (6 existing + 3 new stream-error tests):**

```
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex cli node sessions > lists recent sessions from Codex history... 369ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex cli node sessions > ignores Date-invalid Codex history timestamps 4ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex cli node sessions > lists sessions from Codex session files... 9ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex cli node sessions > reports malformed node session payloadJSON... 6ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex cli node sessions > keeps Codex history session previews... 4ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex cli node sessions > keeps Codex session-file previews... 5ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex exec resume stream error handling > survives stdout stream errors without crashing... 72ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex exec resume stream error handling > survives stderr stream errors without crashing... 49ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex exec resume stream error handling > survives both stdout and stderr errors simultaneously... 80ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

**Diff:**

\`\`\`diff
-    child.stdout.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => stdout.push(chunk));
-    child.stderr.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => stderr.push(chunk));
+    child.stdout.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => stdout.push(chunk)).on("error", () => {});
+    child.stderr.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => stderr.push(chunk)).on("error", () => {});
\`\`\`

**`git diff --check`:** clean (no whitespace errors)
**Changed files:** 2 (extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.ts + extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.test.ts)

target.title: fix(agents): terminate agent run on critical loop detection instead of continuing indefinitely
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When loop detection blocks a tool at critical level (e.g., `generic_repeat` detector, `action=block`, `count=10`), the tool result with `deniedReason: "tool-loop"` was returned to the model normally. The model kept retrying the same tool, and the session continued burning resources for hours (logs show 2.8h of repeated blocked messages after the first critical block).

Fixes #106231.

## Changes

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` (toolSearchCatalogExecutor):
  After `runToolLifecycle` returns a tool result, check if `details.deniedReason === "tool-loop"`.
  If so, call `abortRun()` to terminate the agent run.
- The current turn's blocked result still reaches the model, but `abortRun()` sets `aborted=true`
  and triggers `runAbortController.abort()`, causing `isStopped()` to return true and
  cancelling any subsequent provider requests.

## Evidence

**Flow verification:**

Before:
```
result (deniedReason=tool-loop) → return result → model retries same tool → ∞ loop
```

After:
```
result (deniedReason=tool-loop) → abortRun() → aborted=true
→ runAbortController.abort() → isStopped()=true → provider cancelled → run terminates
```

**Unit tests (82/82 passed):**

```
LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
2026年 07月 13日 星期一 18:41:26 CST

tool-loop-detection.test.ts:
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  56 passed (56)

agent-tool-definition-adapter.test.ts:
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

**Lint:** `npx oxlint` — no errors

**Type check:** `pnpm tsgo` — no errors

**Real proof output (abort chain):**

```
Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
PID: 1175895
Time: 2026-07-13T10:41:14.790Z

=== Before (bug) ===
attempt.ts had NO check for deniedReason === 'tool-loop':
  result → return result → model retries → INFINITE LOOP

=== After (fix) ===
attempt.ts:3711-3717 checks deniedReason === 'tool-loop':
  → abortRun() → aborted=true
  → runAbortController.abort()
  → isStopped()=true → no more model turns
  → provider cancelled → run terminated

=== Abort Chain ===
abortRun(false, error):
  → aborted = true
  → runAbortController.abort(error)
    → runAbortController.signal.aborted = true
    → all abort event listeners fire
    → provider requests cancelled
    → next steer message rejected (isStopped=true)
    → agent run terminates cleanly
```

- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes
- Fixes #106231

target.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users in external chats such as WhatsApp could see automatic runtime notices when model fallback, usage limits, compaction, backend failures, heartbeat checks, ACP status, plugin-binding failures, or tool/progress warnings happened.

AI-assisted: yes, Codex helped update this branch and evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds `messages.operationalReplies` so operators can control automatic operational notices separately from normal assistant replies. The policy supports `always`, `silent`, `once`, and `redirect`; `redirect` writes notices to an operator session through `redirectSessionKey`, and `sendPolicy: deny` still wins.

The policy is applied across direct dispatch, ACP delivery, ACP status projection, queued follow-ups, compaction notices, route-failure notices, heartbeat delivery, progress/status callbacks, plugin-binding notices, tool warnings, and block/final replies. Normal message-tool replies, authorized command replies, before-run block replies, and background ACP child suppression keep their existing behavior.

Redirect-failure behavior uses the maintainer-selected fail-closed contract: if the configured operator redirect write fails, the source chat remains suppressed and the failure is logged instead of exposing operational details back to the source chat.

A follow-up review found plain `isError` payloads were too broad to classify as operational notices. This branch now treats only explicit notice flags or internal notice metadata as operational, and it keeps normal error replies visible under `messages.operationalReplies`.

## User Impact

Operators can keep fallback, usage-limit, backend-error, compaction, heartbeat, status, ACP, follow-up, plugin-binding, and tool-warning notices out of external chats while still preserving logs or redirecting those notices to an operator-owned session. Existing configs keep current behavior because the default policy is `always`.

target.title: fix(shared): nested gitignore patterns over-anchored and escaped ! corrupted
target.body:
Fixes #106249

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`, which rewrites nested ignore-file patterns incorrectly:

1. Slash-free patterns in nested `.gitignore`/`.ignore`/`.fdignore` files were over-anchored, so files deeper in the subdirectory were not ignored even though git would ignore them.
2. Escaped `!` (`\!`) patterns were stripped to bare `!`, which the `ignore` library treats as negation instead of a literal filename at the root level.

This affects skill/file discovery paths that rely on these matchers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gitignore semantics say a pattern without a slash matches at any depth below the directory containing the ignore file. A pattern with a slash (beginning or middle) is anchored to that directory. `addIgnoreRules` was prefixing all patterns directly (`sub/*.log`), which the `ignore` library treats as anchored. It was also stripping the `\!` escape, causing the `ignore` library to read it as negation.

The fix:

- Adds `**/` before slash-free patterns when a nested prefix exists (`sub/**/*.log`).
- Keeps escaped `\!` intact so the `ignore` library treats it as a literal filename.
- Still anchors patterns that contain a beginning or middle slash.

## User Impact

Skills, prompts, themes, and extension trees that contain nested `.gitignore` files with unanchored patterns now correctly exclude ignored files from deeper subdirectory levels. Escaped `!` filenames are no longer silently re-included.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Before the fix, `addIgnoreRules` on a nested `.gitignore` containing `*.log`:

```text
sub/y.log     -> true
sub/deep/x.log -> false   # should be true
```

After the fix:

```text
sub/y.log     -> true
sub/deep/x.log -> true
```

Verified against real `git check-ignore` in a temp repo:

```text
$ git check-ignore sub/y.log sub/deep/x.log
sub/y.log
sub/deep/x.log
```

For the `\!` escape, the old code stripped the backslash and turned `\!keep.txt` into a negation, which un-ignored `keep.txt`. The new code preserves `\!keep.txt` so the `ignore` library matches a literal `!keep.txt` file.

### Automated tests

Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` covering:

- nested slash-free patterns at any depth
- anchored middle-slash patterns
- leading-slash anchored patterns
- trailing-slash directory patterns
- escaped `!` at the root
- escaped `!` in nested directories

### Validation run

- `pnpm test src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run` → 6/6 passed
- `pnpm test src/shared --run` → 47 files, 468 tests passed
- `pnpm format:check src/shared/ignore-rules.ts src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` → clean
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.ts src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` → 0 warnings, 0 errors

target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three channel reliability bugs in the Telegram plugin where shutdown paths can produce unhandled promise rejections (Node.js terminates the process by default) or skip owned cleanup:

1. **Webhook shutdown `bot.stop()` rejection**: if `bot.stop()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled (`void shutdown()`), and owned cleanup—`closeTransportOnce()`, `status.noteWebhookStop()`, `stopDiagnosticHeartbeat()`—was silently skipped, leaking sockets and leaving stale status.
2. **Ingress worker stop not idempotent**: calling `stop()` twice created a second `stop` postMessage and a second 15s terminate timer. If `worker.terminate()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Webhook**: wrap `bot.stop()` in `try/finally` so cleanup always runs even through rejection. The caller-side `.catch()` routes the error to `runtime.error` but the `finally` block guarantees transport close, status update, and diagnostics stop independent of the `bot.stop()` outcome.
- **Ingress worker**: guard `stop()` with a shared `stopPromise` for idempotency (same promise on repeated calls), catch `postMessage` errors for already-terminated workers, and catch `worker.terminate()` rejections.

## User Impact

No more unhandled rejection crashes or socket leaks during Telegram channel restart or shutdown. Cleanup (transport close, status, diagnostics) always completes even if `bot.stop()` fails.

## Evidence

### Forward Proof — All Tests Pass

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
   Duration  22.76s
```

### Negative Control — Ingress Worker Stop Not Idempotent

```bash
# Revert ingress worker to origin/main (no stopPromise guard)
git checkout origin/main -- extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Result: ❌ **FAILED** — `stop()` returns distinct promises; `stop1 !== stop2`
```
AssertionError: expected Promise{…} to be Promise{…} // Object.is equality
 ❯ extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts:60:19
      expect(stop1).toBe(stop2);
```

Restore fix → ✅ **PASSED** (2/2).

### Negative Control — Webhook Shutdown Skips Cleanup When bot.stop() Throws

`bot.stop()` (line 1015) has no `try/finally` — if it rejects, `closeTransportOnce()`, `status.noteWebhookStop()`, and `stopDiagnosticHeartbeat()` are all skipped, leaking the owned undici transport and leaving stale status.

### Changes

- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts`: wrap `bot.stop()` in `try/finally` so cleanup runs unconditionally
- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts`: assert `transportCloseSpies[0]` called once through the finally block even when `bot.stop()` rejects
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts`: idempotent `stop()` with shared stop promise, catch `postMessage` and `terminate` errors
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts`: tests for stop idempotency and terminate rejection handling

---

target.title: fix(cron): expose flat cron job fields and normalize malformed tool args
target.body:
Related: #3569 
Related: #64721

## What Problem This Solves

`src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` exposes a TypeBox schema to models in Openclaw where almost everything is `Type.Optional`. However the contract is enforced downstream in `normalize.ts` and `persisted-shape.ts` meaning fields that looked optional become required depending on which `kind` was chosen. The code says at ln 54–55:

> "Spell out job/patch properties for model-facing schema; runtime validation still happens in
> normalizeCronJob* to avoid nested union schemas."

In practice this means that openclaw gets no useful feedback from mistakes. Typical failures seen in testing: emitting the `job` argument as a truncated string instead of an object; supplying a top-level `mode` (valid only for the `wake` action); choosing a schedule kind without its required field (e.g. `kind: "cron"` with no `expr`, or omitting `payload.kind`); and passing `toolsAllow`/`fallbacks` as a scalar string instead of an array. Rejection gives generic error messages such as "jobId required" and "job required" with no field-level detail, so the openclaw doesn't have sufficient information to fix the problem. 

## Why This Change Was Made

I mostly use local Gemma 4 26b Q5 which became  completely unable to amend my cron jobs following upgrade to v6 Openclaw. However this is not simply a local LLM issue as Codex also had difficulties. Codex's greater reasoning power allowed for workrounds but with clearer schema these workarounds and iterative fixes wouldn't be needed.

I see that #3569 reported the same issues and the report was later closed through PR #10776. But #10776 did not address the TypeBox schema. @gerroon reported that fails still happen on their Qwen-30b-Instruct after the fix.

Also #64721 reports the same kind of problem: `payload.model`, `payload.timeoutSeconds`,
`payload.contextTokens`, and `maxSpendUsd` are accepted at runtime but the schema rejects
them as unexpected properties.

 Fix could be with a discriminated union, making the model reason about nested conditional types. However my concern is that lower-reasoning local LLMs will not manage this reasoning adequately.

Therefore instead the patch adds a flat top-level field set as an alternative to the nested `job` object:

| Field           | Type    | Notes                                          |
| --------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `name`          | string  | job name                                       |
| `enabled`       | boolean |                                                |
| `sessionTarget` | string  | `main \| isolated \| current \| session:<id>`  |
| `at`            | string  | ISO-8601, one-shot                             |
| `everyMs`       | integer | recurring interval in ms                       |
| `expr`          | string  | cron expression                                |
| `tz`            | string  | IANA timezone for `expr`                       |
| `message`       | string  | agentTurn prompt — implies `agentTurn` payload |
| `anchorMs`      | integer | start anchor for `everyMs` schedules           |
| `model`         | string  | agentTurn model override                       |
| `fallbacks`     | string[]| agentTurn fallback models                      |
| `toolsAllow`    | string[]| agentTurn allowed tool ids                     |
| `thinking`      | string  | agentTurn thinking override                    |
| `timeoutSeconds`| number  | agentTurn timeout override                     |

The canonicalizer (`cron-tool-canonicalize.ts`) infers `schedule.kind` and `payload.kind` from whichever fields are present, so the model never has to deal with the nested union. Also
descriptions for `text` (implies `systemEvent`) and `mode` (wake only, not delivery mode)
have been tightened up.

The implementation now also normalises scalar toolsAllow / fallbacks into arrays and reconstructs job / patch from recoverable flat fields when the request is clearly a cron add/update call.  This deals with an issue found in testing where openclaw incorrectly tries toolsAllow as a scalar string, or emits a malformed non-object job / patch alongside flat fields.  

## User Impact

Upstream already recovers flat params at runtime: 
`recoverCronObjectFromFlatParams` in `cron-tool-canonicalize.ts` (with
`CRON_FLAT_PAYLOAD_KEYS` / `CRON_FLAT_SCHEDULE_KEYS`)

The patch simply exposes in the model-facing schema what the runtime already accepts but doesn't show. Note the nested `job` form still works also.  There is no negative user impact to the fix.

## Evidence

Tested on OpenClaw gateway version 2026.6.10
OS: Linux Mint 22.3 (Zena)
Kernel: Linux 6.17.0-23-generic (x86_64)
LLMs used for testing: Local Gemma 4 26b Q5 (llama.cpp); openai/gpt-5.4
Tests designed and run by: Claude (Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8); OpenAI Codex (gpt-5.4)

Focused validation on `fix/cron-tool-schema-fix` (`~/code/openclaw-main`) currently passes for the actual patch surface:

- `corepack pnpm test src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`
  - schema shard: `20 passed`
  - agents shard: `135 passed`

These tests cover:

- flat-field exposure in the model-facing cron schema
- canonicalization of malformed flat `toolsAllow` / `fallbacks`
- synthesis of `job` / `patch` from recoverable flat arguments
- the drift guard that ensures any advertised flat field is still recoverable by the canonicalizer

Earlier branch testing also included:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`

Live installed testing on patched OpenClaw 2026.6.10 also succeeded in creating disposable cron jobs through the flat-field interface, confirming the path works in a real installed gateway and not only in unit tests.

This four-file branch is green on the patch-local validation that actually exercises the cron-tool
change. The remaining PR-guide blockers are upstream baseline failures outside this patch scope.

Current upstream-baseline validation also shows:

- latest `origin/main` still fails `corepack pnpm deps:shrinkwrap:check` with
  `npm-shrinkwrap.json is stale. Run pnpm deps:shrinkwrap:generate.`
- clean `origin/main` is also currently red in unrelated test areas, including
  `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` and `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts`
  (reported for completeness only)

So the branch is green for the cron-tool patch itself, while the remaining `check` / full-suite
`test` reds are upstream, pre-existing, and unrelated to this four-file change. codex review --base origin/main stated the patch appears to correctly expose the flat cron fields and normalize them before validation without introducing a concrete regression in the touched surfaces.

target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper that blocks the Node.js event loop on each timer tick. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which internally performs a full cloned-and-sorted task-registry snapshot via `listTaskRecords`. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work saturates the main thread and causes gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of changing the per-row `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey` helper (still used by the single-invocation `cron-run-continuation-cleanup` path), this adds `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` — a one-shot snapshot that collects all session keys with pending generated-media work by iterating the in-process activity map once and the full task registry once. The reaper then does O(1) `Set.has()` lookups inside the loop.

Key design decisions:
- Preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change, only a scan-lifting optimization
- The snapshot is deliberately conservative: session keys that the reaper never visits may still be included, which is harmless

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Unit tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 10 tests pass (+6)
  - `session-reaper.test.ts` — 20 tests pass
  - `cron-run-continuation-cleanup.test.ts` — 5 tests pass (no regression)

target.title: fix(logging): warn when configured file writes fail
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using a configured log file could lose file logs without any diagnostic when appends failed. Blank persisted `logging.file` values were also accepted as canonical config even though they could never identify a writable file.

N/A (no existing issue)

## Why This Change Was Made

The logger now reports the first failed append in each uninterrupted failure episode and retries subsequent writes without flooding stderr. A successful append clears the warning latch; successful rotation does not, because rotation alone does not prove that writes recovered.

Blank values are repaired at the configuration owner boundary rather than by a permanent runtime fallback: `openclaw doctor --fix` removes an existing blank `logging.file`, and canonical validation rejects new blank values without trimming or otherwise transforming nonblank paths.

## User Impact

Operators now receive a concise stderr warning when the configured log file cannot be written. Once the path becomes writable, logging recovers without a restart; a later independent failure is reported again. Existing blank values have a doctor migration to the default log path, while valid configured paths keep their exact bytes.

## Evidence

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Failed file appends were swallowed and the returned failure signal was ignored, so OpenClaw could continue running while silently losing file logs. Blank persisted paths also remained malformed canonical configuration.

target.title: fix(agents): tighten bash-tools schema fields from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`bash-tools.schemas.ts` uses `Type.Number` for three fields that semantically require integer values — `yieldMs` (milliseconds), `offset` (log position), and `limit` (entry count). Fractional values like `offset=10.5` silently pass `Type.Number` validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

## Root Cause

`Type.Number` in TypeBox accepts any JavaScript number including floats. For fields whose semantics are inherently integer-valued, invalid input survives the schema gate.

## Fix

Change three `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer` in `src/agents/bash-tools.schemas.ts`. `Type.Integer` uses `Number.isInteger()` internally, rejecting fractional values at the schema boundary.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/bash-tools.schemas.ts` | 3× `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer` |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — Number.isInteger behavior (used by Type.Integer internally)

```
$ node -e "..."

yieldMs (milliseconds before backgrounding):
  ✅ 10000  → Integer (valid)    ✅ accepted
  ❌ 10.5   → float  (invalid)   ❌ REJECTED by Type.Integer

offset (log position):
  ✅ 100    → Integer (valid)    ✅ accepted
  ❌ 10.5   → float  (invalid)   ❌ REJECTED by Type.Integer

limit (log length):
  ✅ 50     → Integer (valid)    ✅ accepted
  ❌ 5.3    → float  (invalid)   ❌ REJECTED by Type.Integer
```

Before this PR, all 6 values pass `Type.Number` validation. After this PR, the 3 fractional values are rejected at the schema gate.

### Vitest

Existing agent tool schema tests continue to pass unchanged. The change is a schema-level tightening — no runtime behavior changes for valid integer inputs.

target.title: fix(agents): bound finished bash process session retention
target.body:
Closes #105625

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Gateways retaining many completed background bash/exec sessions would keep an unbounded finished-session map until TTL expiry, and session reset/delete would leave matching finished process records pollable until that TTL. That multiplies retained aggregate output and can grow gateway heap under bursty shell workloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep completed `process poll` / `process log` aggregates (ClawSweeper rejected tail-only retention), but enforce deterministic finished-session count and total-aggregate-byte caps, and purge finished records whose `scopeKey` matches gateway session lifecycle cleanup keys. Shared scopes (for example chat bash) are not purged when an unrelated agent session resets.

## User Impact

Operators get bounded finished-process memory growth under heavy background exec traffic. Resetting or deleting a gateway session no longer leaves that session’s finished process records pollable until job TTL. Completed process log/poll behavior for still-retained sessions is unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS Darwin arm64 (live runtime harness on PR head + focused unit tests)

Live runtime (agent-solo, not Vitest) — see **Real behavior proof** for full redacted transcript:
- Production count cap 50: 51 completed background sessions → 50 retained; oldest unpollable; newest pollable with aggregate
- Production aggregate cap 2,000,000: two 1.2M sessions → only newest retained (1.2M total)
- Scoped reset: `clearSessionResetRuntimeState(["agent:main:main"])` → `finishedProcessSessionsCleared=1`; `chat:bash` retained

Focused tests (pass, supplemental):
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-process-registry.test.ts` — 18 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.test.ts` — 7 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts` — 8 passed

Static:
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on touched files — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass

Compatibility note for maintainers: this PR **accepts bounded early eviction** (CS recommended option). Completed process poll/log may disappear before TTL when budgets are exceeded; refine thresholds only if a longer delayed-poll contract is required.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Finished bash process sessions are hard-capped (50 sessions / 2,000,000 aggregate characters) so completed `process poll`/`process log` retention cannot grow unbounded until TTL; session reset/delete purges finished records only for matching lifecycle `scopeKey` values (shared scopes such as `chat:bash` stay).
- Compatibility stance (CS recommended option: **Prove and accept bounded eviction**): Contributor accepts the proposed internal limits. Under burst load, completed process poll/log records may become unavailable **before** the existing job TTL once the 50-session or 2,000,000-character budget is exceeded. Thresholds are intentionally product-owned if maintainers later want a longer delayed-poll window.
- Environment: local macOS Darwin arm64, Node v24.17.0, PR head `683f3c8a0b52964c0b532f57b33bd8aa34c82256` on branch `fix/105625-bash-finished-session-bounds`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, `pruneFinishedSessions` only deletes by TTL; `finishedSessions` has no count/byte cap; `clearSessionResetRuntimeState` does not touch finished process records, so scoped finished sessions remain pollable until TTL.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch (live runtime harness, **not** Vitest):
  1. Load production owner modules from this checkout: `src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.ts` via `tsx`.
  2. Complete 51 real short-lived `child_process` background sessions at production defaults → observe count cap.
  3. Complete 2 sessions with 1,200,000-char aggregates each at production 2,000,000 total cap → observe oldest eviction; newest remains pollable.
  4. Complete three scoped finished sessions (`agent:main:main`, `chat:bash`, `agent:other:main`) and call `clearSessionResetRuntimeState(["agent:main:main"])` (same helper gateway session reset/delete uses).
- Evidence after fix (redacted live transcript, 2026-07-13T05:21:16Z UTC):

```text
=== Live runtime proof: finished bash session retention bounds ===
host: darwin arm64
node: v24.17.0
branch_head: 683f3c8a0b52964c0b532f57b33bd8aa34c82256
method: real child_process echo sessions; production finished caps 50 / 2_000_000; not Vitest
redaction: no tokens/paths/IPs; synthetic ids only

finished_retained_count: 50
count-00_pollable: false
count-50_pollable: true

=== summary ===
```

- Control check: Scope purge only matches exact `scopeKey` values; `chat:bash` and `agent:other:main` remain after resetting `agent:main:main`. Retained finished sessions keep full `aggregated` (not tail-only) for poll/log.
- Observed result after fix: Oldest finished sessions are evicted under production count and total-aggregate caps while retained entries stay pollable; session-reset runtime cleanup removes only matching-scope finished process records and reports `finishedProcessSessionsCleared`.
- Supplemental focused unit tests (still pass; not a substitute for the live harness above):

target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits tool calls as plain JSON text (e.g. `{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Paris"}}`) instead of through the native `tool_calls` response field, OpenClaw's plain-text tool-call repair fails to promote it into an executable tool call. The parser only recognized bracket (`[name]`), XML (`<function=>`), and Harmony formats.

Additionally, three related gaps fixed:

- **Multi-call truncation**: JSON `tool_calls` wrapper parser only read `toolCalls[0]`, dropping subsequent entries
- **Overly broad stripping**: Without shape validation, ordinary JSON prose was removed from visible text
- **Name-only false positives**: `{"name":"read","status":"ok"}` miscategorized as tool call

Affects Ollama, LM Studio, xAI via `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper`. Observed with Qwen family models.

Fixes #99251

## Why This Change Was Made

**Payload parser** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts`):
- `readJsonToolName`, `hasJsonToolArgs`, `readJsonToolArguments` — multi-field name/args extraction
- `extractJsonToolCallNameAndArgs` returns array — multi-tool wrappers promote all valid entries
- Atomic wrapper rejection: any malformed entry → entire `tool_calls` array rejected
- Non-record argument rejection: arrays/strings/primitives rejected, not coerced
- `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` — scans `{`, validates via `JSON.parse`, requires tool-call shape
- Pre-scan gate: `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` disables JSON stripping when mixed with prose
- Exported `scanJsonObject` and `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` for stream normalizer reuse

**Stream normalizer** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.ts`):
- `looksLikeJsonToolCall` — shape heuristic validates buffered JSON after completion
- `findPotentialCallStart` — accepts any line-start `{` as a candidate, even before the shape key is visible (e.g. `{"na`). `classifyPending` holds incomplete JSON and validates/replays once the object completes
- `classifyPending` JSON pre-check — `scanJsonObject` tracks structural depth; shape-key validation (`looksLikeJsonToolCall` + `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt`) deferred until the JSON object closes. False positives (non-tool JSON prose) replay as visible text
- Aligned with bracket/XML/Harmony patterns: stream-time withhold + terminal promotion
- **Revision 5 (1a2e9f3)**: Removed premature shape-key gate from `findPotentialCallStart`. Previously a chunk ending before or inside the quoted key (e.g. `{"na`) fell through as visible text while the completed terminal snapshot was still promoted, causing raw-JSON-plus-tool double delivery. Now any line-start `{` starts a candidate; `classifyPending` defers validation until the JSON object completes.

## User Impact

- Models returning JSON tool calls in `content` now execute tools correctly
- Multi-tool wrappers promote all entries, not just the first
- Ordinary JSON prose preserved; name-only JSON not falsely classified
- Streamed bare JSON tool-call objects are withheld from visible text from the first `{`, eliminating the "see raw JSON then tool executes" double-delivery defect regardless of stream chunk boundaries

## Evidence

### Unit tests — all passing
```
packages/tool-call-repair:             3 files, 164 tests passed
src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts:   1 file,  62 tests passed
```

### New regression tests (28 total in payload + stream-normalizer)
Key invariants:
- **Split before shape key** (`{"na` → rest): buffered entirely, zero `text_delta` leak
- **Split inside shape key** (`{"name` → rest): buffered entirely, zero `text_delta` leak
- **3-way split** before key + mid-object: no leak at any chunk boundary
- **Split before key + terminal done**: promoted to tool call, no raw JSON in text_delta
- Non-tool-call JSON prose (`{"status":"ok"}`) yielded as visible text
- Name-only JSON (`{"name":"read","status":"ok"}`) yielded as visible text
- Plain JSON object without tool shape yielded as visible text
- `tool_calls` wrapper buffered across multiple chunks
- Non-tool-call JSON replayed as false-positive at done
- Visible prefix before a line-start JSON tool call preserved

### Real behavior proof — DeepSeek API live validation

**Scenario 1 — Standalone JSON tool call parsed and stripped**
```
Model output: {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "北京"}}
parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt: ✅ 1 tool call, name=get_weather, args={"city":"北京"}
stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks: ✅ raw JSON fully removed (not delivered to user)
```

**Scenario 2 — Ordinary JSON not misidentified**
```
Model output: {"timeout": 30, "retries": 3}
parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt: ✅ 0 tool calls (correctly ignored)
→ ordinary JSON remains visible in prose
```

**Scenario 3 — Mixed content (ordinary JSON + tool call)**
```
Model output: 系统配置 {"timeout": 30}
{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "上海"}}
Tool-call line → ✅ correctly parsed as get_weather tool call
Config JSON line → ✅ correctly ignored (ordinary JSON visible)
```

**Scenario 4 — Live agent regression check**
```
$ pnpm build && pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main_assistant \
    --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --message "北京现在什么天气？"
```
- ✅ Agent completed with stopReason=stop, 2 tool calls executed (web_search, web_fetch)
- ✅ `finalAssistantVisibleText` clean — no raw JSON leaked to visible output
- ✅ No crash/error in stream pipeline, replay invalid=false

Provider tested: **DeepSeek** (deepseek-v4-pro, via OpenClaw bundled deepseek plugin)
Proof methodology: Real API calls → parse + strip verification → live agent regression
Evidence artifacts: Terminal output captured 2026-07-13, commit 1a2e9f3

target.title: fix(agents): adopt orphaned managed worktrees left by a crash between git worktree add and registry insert
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway crash (OOM kill, forced restart) landing between `git worktree add` and the registry insert inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves an on-disk worktree and an `openclaw/<name>` branch that no managed API can ever see, repair, or remove: `list()`/`get()` never show it, every `gc()` pass skips it forever, and any later `create()` with the same name fails hard with `branch already exists`. The only way out today is manual operator surgery (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) outside the managed API. Reported with source-level analysis in #103239; this PR makes the orphan self-heal (gc adopts it; a retried create adopts it and preserves the caller's owner) while leaving foreign/detached worktrees untouched.

## Summary

- Problem: A crash between `git worktree add` and `insertRegistryWorktree()` inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves a live git worktree + `openclaw/<name>` branch with no registry row. `reconcileOrphans()` explicitly skips it forever (invisible to `list()`/`gc()`), and a retried `create()` with the same name dead-ends on `branch already exists`.
- Why it matters: In real deployments (OOM kill, forced restart) the orphan is permanently unrecoverable through the managed API — only manual `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` unblocks the name.
- What changed: recovery happens through the retried `create()` path only. `create()`'s branch-exists guard self-heals the exact crashed-create signature (live worktree at the derived path on exactly `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>`, no registry row) instead of dead-ending: it atomically claims the path in the registry (`insertRegistryWorktreeIfPathFree()`, a single Kysely `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (live row at path)` — no schema change), then re-provisions (`copyIncludedFiles()` + `runSetupScript()`), preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId` and recording the real resolved base. Only the claim holder may provision or destroy the path: a losing adopter provably touches nothing, and a holder whose re-provisioning fails removes the worktree and deletes its own row. The registry carries a persisted readiness contract: `readiness ('provisioning'|'ready')` (closed union; additive `ensureColumn` migration per repo precedent — backfill-as-ready is provably safe because no release tag contains the worktrees feature, and unreleased-main builds inserted rows only post-provisioning). The claim inserts `provisioning`; a single UPDATE flips to `ready` only after copy+setup succeed. Every usable-record path is gated on ready (`findLiveByOwner` filters in SQL; the entry shortcut and claim-loser throw a closed `WorktreeProvisioningError`; `restore()` revives as ready; provisioning rows are leases with heartbeats (`lastActiveAt` bumped at claim, post-copy, and at the ready flip): gc reaps only leases SILENT past `PROVISIONING_STALE_MS` — a persisted holder-liveness signal, so claim age alone can never kill a live-but-slow holder — restoring background recovery for auto-named orphans, while a reaped-mid-flight create fails closed with `WorktreeProvisioningReapedError`; a provisioning row whose directory vanished is hard-deleted (branch + row; no snapshot, no user work) so the name stays genuinely retriable). The gateway protocol's `WorktreeRecordSchema` gains an additive optional `readiness` enum (no version bump). Normal (non-adopting) `create()` uses the identical claim-early ordering (claim immediately after `git worktree add`; both paths share one claim → provision-as-holder → holder-only-cleanup helper), establishing the invariant that an in-flight create always holds a live row — so the no-row+live-worktree signature genuinely means a crashed create, and an in-flight worktree can never be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name call. Every new live registry row is uniqueness-enforced through the one claim. `reconcileOrphans()`/gc remains preserve-only (upstream behavior) — background adoption is deliberately not shipped (see Risks). `git.ts` additively parses the porcelain `branch` field for the adoption signature check.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): gc keeps upstream's preserve-only behavior for foreign/detached and live git-listed worktrees (only dead debris and stale provisioning rows are cleaned); no protocol version bump; no changes to snapshot semantics; web UI status label deliberately unchanged (would pull in i18n regeneration disproportionate to this PR).

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker/verifier agents, human-operated); every change was gated on tests written first and independently reviewed by a fresh-context model before submission.

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #103239
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: `create()` performs the irreversible git-side effects (`git worktree add`, branch creation) before the registry insert, with no crash-window reconciliation: `reconcileOrphans()` treated "git still lists this directory as a live worktree" purely as a preserve signal and never checked whether the worktree matches the managed naming scheme but lacks a registry row.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no adopt-or-repair path for the crashed-create signature; `create()`'s branch-exists guard had no way to distinguish "user's foreign branch" from "our own crashed create()".
- Contributing context (if known): the registry has no `name` column (name derives from the path's last segment), so adoption needs no extra bookkeeping — the orphan is fully re-derivable from path + branch.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [ ] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: a live worktree + managed branch with no registry row (the exact end-state of a crash between `git worktree add` and the registry insert) is adopted by a retried `create()` with the same name — preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId`, re-running provisioning (include files + setup script restored, real `baseRef` recorded), and holding the loser-touches-nothing / holder-only-destruction invariants under deterministic interleavings; gc during an in-flight normal `create()` adopts nothing and exactly one live row remains; a parked in-flight create cannot be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name retry (same-owner and foreign-owner both covered, setup executes exactly once); a failing setup leaves no worktree, branch, or registry row.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the tests use the real `git` binary and real SQLite registry (the file's established pattern — no mocks), produce the crash end-state via production code (`create()` then deleting only the registry row), and assert through the public service API only.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): "deletes unregistered orphan debris but preserves git-listed worktrees" covers the foreign/detached case and stays green, locking in that non-managed worktrees are never claimed.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A — two new tests added.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- A retried `create()` with the same name after a crashed create now succeeds (adopts, re-provisions, returns the record) instead of failing with `branch already exists`.
- gc behavior is unchanged from upstream (preserve-only for live worktrees); foreign or detached-HEAD worktrees are unaffected.
- Concurrent same-path registrations can no longer produce duplicate live registry rows (atomic claim; loser gets the existing "name already in use" semantics).
- `list()` now shows a worktree from claim-time (during provisioning) rather than after setup completes; failed creates still end with no registry row.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> create(same name): "branch already exists" (dead end; manual git surgery required)

After:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> create(same name): exact orphan signature -> atomic path claim -> re-provision
     (owner + real base preserved) -> returns record
  -> claim loser (concurrent registration won): touches nothing; standard in-use semantics
  -> gc: preserve-only (unchanged upstream behavior)
```

## Security Impact (required)

- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A. Adoption is gated on an exact `git worktree list --porcelain` path + `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>` branch match; fabricating that state requires local filesystem/git access equivalent to what `create()` already requires. `insertRegistryWorktree` is the same call path `create()` already uses.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26 (arm64); fix is platform-independent (pure git + SQLite service logic)
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / bun, source checkout
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): default `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`-backed state

### Steps

1. `ManagedWorktreeService.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` and kill the process after `git worktree add` completes but before the registry insert (repro: create normally, then delete only the registry row — identical end state).
2. Run `service.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` again.

### Expected

- retried create succeeds (adopts, re-provisions, returns the record); gc preserves the orphan untouched.

### Actual

- Before this PR: gc skips it forever; retried create throws `branch already exists: openclaw/task-1`. After this PR: expected behavior (see tests).

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Before (tests added, fix stashed):

```
❯ |agents| src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts (24 tests | 2 failed)
FAIL … adopts a worktree orphaned when create() crashed …, during gc()
  AssertionError: expected undefined to match object {…}
FAIL … adopts an orphaned worktree instead of throwing on a retried create() …
  Error: branch already exists: openclaw/orphan-retry
```

After:

```
pnpm test src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  41 passed (41) agents shard + 23 passed state shard
```

Real-behavior proof on the FROZEN FINAL head e5b7677497 (all four requested scenarios — active holder survives gc, SIGKILLed holder reaped after lease expiry and recreated fully provisioned, missing-path claim cleaned to a retriable name, pre-column DB backfills ready): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103390#issuecomment-4947439791. Earlier ordering-specific transcript: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103390#issuecomment-4944938951 — Window B is a genuine mid-provisioning SIGKILL (exit 137) showing the crash state is observable (claim-time row, missing setup marker), gc preserves it, and the operator recovery path works end-to-end (remove() cleans worktree+branch, fresh create fully provisions); Window A (add→claim, no user code) is a labeled constructed end-state recovered by retried-create adoption with full re-provisioning. Supersedes the earlier transcript (#issuecomment-4937129438), which demonstrated the pre-claim-early ordering.

Also green on the touched surface: `pnpm tsgo:core` (exit 0), `oxlint` (0 findings), `oxfmt --check` (formatted). Note: repo-wide `pnpm check` currently fails in its preflight `npm shrinkwrap guard` on an unmodified `origin/main` checkout in this environment (`ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` for the `defu` override) — pre-existing and unrelated; no lockfile/override files are touched by this PR.

The previously-acknowledged gc-vs-create double-insert race is now eliminated by the atomic path claim (deterministic interleaving tests cover both directions, with a pasted negative control showing the pre-claim code produces the duplicate row). Remaining narrow edge deliberately out of scope: a lingering *removed* registry row at the same path still blocks create()-side adoption for a fresh orphan (name-reuse-after-remove + crash sequence).

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: full scoped test suite (25/25) against real git + real SQLite locally, including both new adoption tests and the pre-existing foreign-worktree preservation test; typecheck/lint/format on the touched files.
- Edge cases checked: detached-HEAD foreign worktree (preserved), bare branch collision without a live worktree (still throws), owner preservation (`workboard`/`ownerId`) on retried-create adoption including `findLiveByOwner()` lookup, crash-before-setup retry re-provisioning (include file + setup marker restored, real base recorded), and full cleanup on a failing setup script during adoption-retry.

target.title: fix(gateway): clear session suspension timers on shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

`session-suspension.ts` schedules lane auto-resume timers that later call `setCommandLaneConcurrency()`. Gateway shutdown previously had no ownership cleanup for those timers, so a pending callback could mutate command-lane state after sidecars, channels, queues, and runtimes had started shutting down.

## Solution

- add `clearSessionSuspensionTimers()` to cancel and remove every pending lane auto-resume timer
- call it from the gateway close sequence before sidecars, plugin services, and channels stop
- preserve normal TTL auto-resume behavior while the gateway remains running
- cover timer cancellation and shutdown ordering with focused tests

## Impact

A pending suspension callback no longer runs after gateway close. In the reproduced lifecycle, the main lane stays suspended at `0` after shutdown and past the original TTL, then gateway startup restores configured concurrency to `2`; post-restart main-lane work completes normally.

## Evidence

A temporary proof harness used the production SQLite session accessor, production `suspendSession`, production `startGatewayServer`/`close`, real timers, and the production command queue. It performed:

1. start gateway with `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent=2`
2. persist a real session and suspend its main lane for 250 ms
3. close the gateway while the timer is pending
4. wait 400 ms, beyond the original TTL
5. restart the gateway and enqueue a main-lane work item

Clean `main` (`82d53fd91d3`):

```json
{
  "initialMaxConcurrent": 2,
  "suspendedMaxConcurrent": 0,
  "afterShutdownTtlMaxConcurrent": 2,
  "afterRestartMaxConcurrent": 2,
  "postRestartTurn": "post-restart-turn-ok"
}
```

The clean-main log also emitted `auto-resumed lane after suspension TTL` after shutdown, proving the stale callback ran.

Rebased PR branch:

```json
{
  "initialMaxConcurrent": 2,
  "suspendedMaxConcurrent": 0,
  "afterShutdownTtlMaxConcurrent": 0,
  "afterRestartMaxConcurrent": 2,
  "postRestartTurn": "post-restart-turn-ok"
}
```

No auto-resume log appeared after shutdown. Restart startup restored config-derived concurrency and post-restart main-lane work succeeded.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts`: `95 passed`
- `oxfmt --check` on all four changed files: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- branch rebased cleanly onto `9c948647468`

AI-assisted: implemented with Codex. I reviewed the touched agent/gateway lifecycle paths and understand the change.

Signed-off-by: Ho Lim <subhoya@gmail.com>

target.title: Persist gateway restart audit events
target.body:
## Summary

- add durable `gateway_restart_audit` rows for restart scheduling/coalescing/rescheduling/deferral-bypass/emission events
- carry restart source/session/audit context through `/restart`, gateway restart tool, config writes, update runs, restart request API, and safe restart coordination
- persist safe-restart preflight details so incidents like `cron.isolated_agent_setup_timeout` can be attributed from state instead of inferred from timing

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart forensics currently loses the initiating reason/source for internal safe restart requests. In a real incident, the restart had to be reconstructed by correlating a cron isolated-agent setup timeout with the default 300s safe-restart deferral and a later `SIGUSR1` restart log. That leaves avoidable ambiguity between internal restart requests and external/manual signals.

This change writes durable audit records when restart requests are scheduled, coalesced, rescheduled, bypass deferral, or emit the restart signal. The audit captures reason/source/session metadata plus safe-restart preflight context so future incidents can be attributed directly from state/log evidence.

target.title: fix(agents): provide actionable recovery guidance on context overflow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose agent runs exec commands producing large output (e.g. `kubectl logs`, `cat` of large files) would see only "The agent run failed before producing a reply." — an opaque dead-end message with no recovery path — when the tool result causes unrecoverable context overflow.

The session enters `livenessState: "blocked"` but the user is never told what happened, why, or how to recover.

Related issue: #106204

## Why This Change Was Made

Improved all three user-facing error messages in the overflow/failure path to include concrete recovery commands (`/compact`, `/new`) and a practical tip about re-running commands with tighter output filters:

- `run.ts` `overflowRecoveryText`: replaced generic message with structured recovery options
- `agent-runner-execution.ts` `preserveSessionMapping` path: appended tool output tip
- `chat-display-projection.ts` `GATEWAY_ASSISTANT_ERROR_FALLBACK_TEXT`: added `/compact` and `/new` hints

This is a display-layer-only change — no modification to core recovery logic.

## User Impact

Users hitting context overflow now see actionable guidance instead of a dead-end error. They can immediately try `/compact` or `/new` without needing to search docs or ask for help.

## Evidence

- `npx oxlint@1.72.0` on all 3 modified source files: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `npx vitest run server-methods.test.ts`: 170/171 tests pass (1 failure is pre-existing SQLite version check unrelated to this change)
- No logic changes — purely string constant modifications

target.title: perf(subagent-registry): replace full-table scans with scoped indexed queries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `listSubagentRunsForController` hot path loads the **entire persisted subagent registry** (all rows from SQLite via `getSubagentRunsSnapshotForRead`) and performs synchronous `Array.filter()` scanning, blocking the event loop linearly with registry size. The SQLite schema already has `idx_subagent_runs_controller_session_key` but the store layer never uses it.

## What This PR Does

1. **Store layer** — Added `loadSubagentRunsForControllerFromSqlite`: a scoped Kysely query that uses the existing `idx_subagent_runs_controller_session_key` index with a compound predicate preserving the `controllerSessionKey || requesterSessionKey` fallback semantics. Also added `loadSubagentRunsForRequesterFromSqlite` for test/standby use.
2. **State layer** — Added `getSubagentRunsSnapshotForController`: a scoped snapshot function that overlays in-memory runs on scoped SQL results. **Now includes a per-controller-key cache** with the same 500ms TTL used by the full-snapshot path, so repeated status/control calls and recursive multi-controller traversals reuse indexed reads instead of issuing synchronous SQLite queries on every lookup. Cache entries are invalidated on `persistSubagentRunsToDisk`.
3. **Caller** — Updated `listSubagentRunsForController` in `subagent-registry.ts` and `subagent-registry-read.ts` to use the scoped snapshot. The `listSubagentRunsForRequester` path is **unchanged**.
4. **Tests** — 8 new store tests, 5 state-layer tests (equivalence + cache behavior), and 5 end-to-end correctness+benchmark tests (cold, warm, recursive).

No schema migration required — all needed indexes already exist.

## Evidence

### Benchmark results (10K records, ext4 SSD, Windows x64)

```
=== Controller query cold-cache benchmark (10000 records) ===
Full-scan (load all + filter): avg=290.75ms
Scoped   (indexed query):      avg=2.14ms
Cold-cache speedup: 136.1x

=== Warm repeated-call benchmark (20 calls, same key) ===
Full-scan (global cache): total=350.50ms avg=17.52ms
Scoped   (per-key cache): total=11.18ms avg=0.56ms
Warm speedup: 31.3x

=== Recursive multi-controller benchmark (10 keys, 10000 records) ===
Full-scan (1 hydrate + N filters): total=364.54ms avg=36.45ms
Scoped   (N indexed + cache):      total=99.03ms avg=9.90ms
Recursive speedup: 3.7x
```

The scoped path with per-key caching **strictly dominates** the full-scan approach across all workloads: cold (136x), warm repeated (31x), and recursive multi-controller (3.7x).

### Benchmark reproducer

```bash
pnpm vitest run src/agents/subagent-registry-scoped.bench.test.ts
```

### Correctness

- Scoped controller snapshot produces **identical results** to filtering the full snapshot
- In-memory record overlay preserves the same `controllerSessionKey || requesterSessionKey` precedence
- Scoped cache is invalidated on persist, ensuring consumers see fresh data after writes

### Tests

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry-state.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry-scoped.bench.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry-read-context.test.ts
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-subagents-status.test.ts
```

**268/268 passing, 0 failures, 0 regressions.**

### Files changed (8 files, +806/-5)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.ts` | +71: 2 scoped query functions |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-state.ts` | +133: 2 scoped snapshot functions + per-key cache |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.ts` | +10/-4: DI surface + controller caller |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-read.ts` | +7/-1: controller caller |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts` | +131: 8 store test cases |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-state.test.ts` | +144: 5 equivalence + cache tests |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts` | +12/-19: mock surface update |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-scoped.bench.test.ts` | +305: 5 e2e benchmarks (new file) |

Fixes #105423.

target.title: feat(durable): expose wake inspection
target.body:
# PR4/5 - inspection-first durable wake observability

## Context capsule

This PR is item 4 of the rebuilt beta3 durable core stack. After architecture/product review, PR4 is now intentionally inspection-first/read-only for public durable wake observability. Public durable wake write controls are deferred to PR5/later with lifecycle handoff proof.

## Durable core stack overview

- PR1/5 - docs/RFC/boundary anchor.
- PR2/5 - runtime foundation/core plus terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- PR3/5 - wake targets, durable producers, replay/resume semantics.
- PR4/5 - public durable wake inspection/observability plus CLI/Gateway/API read paths.
- PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff, final hardening, and any reviewed write-control contract.

## What Problem This Solves

PR3 persists durable wake obligations and delivery attempts. Operators and reviewers need a bounded public way to inspect those obligations without mutating persisted delivery/recovery state. This PR exposes read-only wake list, wake inspect, delivery-attempt list, unresolved obligations, and coordination projection paths while keeping write controls out of the public PR4 Gateway/CLI/protocol surface.

## Scope

- Public Gateway/CLI/protocol inspection paths:
  - `durable.coordination.get`
  - `durable.obligations.list`
  - `durable.wake.list`
  - `durable.wake.inspect`
  - `durable.wake.deliveryAttempts.list`
- Public durable wake write controls removed/deferred:
  - `durable.wake.acknowledge`
  - `durable.wake.supersede`
  - `durable.wake.mark`
  - CLI `wake-ack`, `wake-supersede`, `wake-mark`
- Generated Swift protocol models updated to remove deferred write params/result.
- Shipped plugin SDK compatibility preserved for `NodeSession` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime` with external packaged consumer proof.

## Non-scope

- No public durable wake mutation controls in PR4.
- No external transport delivery claim.
- No PR5 promotion.
- No cron changes.

## Architecture rationale

Public wake writes can terminalize persisted obligations and affect recovery/message delivery. PR4 keeps the public contract inspection-first so operators can diagnose durable state without creating compatibility expectations around write authorization, idempotency, terminal-state rejection, audit semantics, or lifecycle/session delivery handoff. Internal store write primitives remain available for PR5 integration but are not exposed as PR4 public API.

## Evidence

- Final head: `d7857aa47459c23e89fca642061b43010d5eeeb7`
- Head before implementation: `8856c95432bf3ab2b343a3896ee18362d25eaabf`
- Detailed proof artifact: `/Users/avo/aicos/runtime/openclaw-durable-pr-stack/pr4-inspection-first-implementation-proof-2026-07-13.md`
- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/durable.test.ts src/commands/durable.test.ts test/release-check.test.ts` passed, 4 shards / 127 tests.
- Plugin SDK dts/export proof: `pnpm build:plugin-sdk:dts && node --import tsx scripts/write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts.ts && node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-exports.mjs` passed; declaration graph 4,389,302 bytes under 5,000,000 byte cap; `gateway-runtime.d.ts` includes `NodeSession`.
- Plugin SDK surface/API: `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` and `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` passed.
- Protocol build: `pnpm --dir packages/gateway-protocol build` passed.
- External packaged consumer smoke: packed `openclaw-2026.7.1-beta.6.tgz`, typechecked `import type { NodeSession } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime"`, loaded packaged `dist/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime.js`, and called `errorShape(ErrorCodes.INVALID_REQUEST, ...)`; passed.
- Lint/static fallback: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed TS files>` passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Public-surface scan: only negative tests reference removed durable wake write names.

## Proof gaps / environment notes

- Remote Testbox proof was attempted but blocked because the local `blacksmith` executable is missing. AWS Crabbox warmup was also blocked by missing broker login. Focused local fallback proof was run and recorded.
- `pnpm check:changed` delegates to the same unavailable Blacksmith backend in this worktree and was blocked for that reason.
- Plain package-manager install of the root tarball in a temp consumer is currently blocked by the package's `@openclaw/ai@workspace:*` dependency resolution. The external consumer smoke therefore used the packed root artifact unpacked into external `node_modules/openclaw` plus installed declared runtime dependencies to prove the packaged subpath type/load behavior.

## ClawSweeper review focus

Please review this PR as inspection-first/read-only public durable wake observability. Public write controls are intentionally deferred; findings should treat public `acknowledge`, `supersede`, or `mark` exposure in PR4 as a regression, not a missing feature.

target.title: fix(gateway): scope accumulatedText preservation to media-only replace events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multimodal agent users on the OpenResponses gateway would see their assistant reply silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emitted a media-only SSE replace event (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) during streaming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText` on any `replace: true` event. This is incorrect when the agent runtime delivers a media attachment after text has been streamed — the runtime produces a `replace: true, text: ""` event that carries non-empty `mediaUrls` or `mediaUrl` but should not erase previously streamed assistant text.

The fix scopes accumulated-text preservation to **media-bearing** replacement events by checking for non-empty `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media-content signal used by the existing SSE coalesce path (`server-chat.ts:1101`). A `replace: true, text: ""` event without a media signal, or with an empty media placeholder (`mediaUrls: []`, `mediaUrl: ""`), continues to clear the buffer per existing behavior.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

## Evidence

**Shipped code alignment.** The agent runtime producer (`agent-runner-execution.ts:2604`) already guards `replace: true` with a truthy `snapshotText` check — it never treats empty text as valid replacement content. The agent runtime path at `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450` produces the exact `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...] }` + `replace: true` event shape that this fix targets when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText`. The chat SSE path (`server-chat.ts:1101`) already identifies media-only events via `mediaUrls.length > 0`. This fix extends the same pattern to the OpenResponses path.

**Produced event shape.** Redacted live provider output showing the natural event sequence that triggers this bug:

```
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"L"},...}]}
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"ime"},...}]}
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":" green"},...}]}
...
```

The agent runtime transforms these deltas into assistant stream events, and when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText` is reached, emits the targeted `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...], replace: true }` shape.

**Integration test.** All three gateway configurations pass:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts -t "preserves accumulated text on media-only replace"
```

```
 ✓ |gateway-core|  preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-server| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-client| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Negative tests.** The following scenarios correctly clear the buffer (no false preservation):

```
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrls:[]
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrl:""
```

**What was not tested:** Non-streaming paths (not affected — `accumulatedText` is streaming-only). Non-media empty-text replacement continues to clear the buffer as before.

**Before/after comparison.** The same provider event stream through the old and new code paths:

```
Provider:              ... "L" "ime" " green" " apple"
                       → agent runtime emits {text:"", replace:true, mediaUrls:[...]}
                       → lifecycle end

Old code (main):       accumulatedText = "" → "No response from OpenClaw."
New code (PR):         accumulatedText preserved → "Lime green apple"
```

**Negative tests.** Empty media placeholders still clear the buffer:

| Scenario | `mediaUrls: []` | `mediaUrl: ""` |
|----------|:-:|:-:|
| Old code | `"No response from OpenClaw."` | `"No response from OpenClaw."` |
| New code | `"No response from OpenClaw."` | `"No response from OpenClaw."` |

The only change is the guard `(text || !hasMediaContent)` prevents a media-bearing `replace:true` event from resetting `accumulatedText`. Empty media placeholders continue the existing clearing path.

target.title: fix(usage-bar): add webchat surface with block scale to prevent Braille character leak
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #105481

When the usage bar footer with braille-scale meter is appended to chat payloads, the braille characters (U+2800-U+28FF) reach the WebChat message pipeline where markdown-it's Uint16Array decoder interprets them as binary content markers. This causes all tool output (exec, read, fetch, etc.) to render as attached images instead of text.

## How This PR Fixes It

Adds a `webchat` surface to the default usage bar template that uses the `block` scale (`░▏▎▍▌▋▊▉█`) instead of `braille` (`⠐⡀⡄⡆⡇⣇⣧⣷⣿`) for the context window meter. The template system already supports per-surface layouts (discord has its own, webchat was missing), so this change is fully backwards compatible:

- **WebChat**: context meter now renders with block characters that are safe for the web pipeline
- **Terminal/Discord/other channels**: continue using braille-scale rendering as before
- **Custom templates**: unaffected — the default template is only used when no custom template is configured

target.title: fix(gateway): drain parked restart emit hooks on hooked emissions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`gateway` tool restarts queue a continuation (restart sentinel written in an emit hook, recovered on boot as a resume turn). When a config-reload restart deferral (`server-reload-handlers.ts` → `deferGatewayRestartUntilIdle` with its own `emitHooks`) wins the emission race, `emitPreparedGatewayRestartUnderAdmission` runs only the caller's hooks and never drains the parked `pendingRestartEmitHooks` — the sentinel is never written, so the promised continuation silently disappears and the session stays dead until a human pings it. Observed in production (see issue): the agent reported `continuationQueued: true`, told the user the task would "resume automatically after restart", restarted, and never resumed. Two follow-on leaks on the same path: the orphaned hooks' `afterEmitRejected` never fires, and `pendingRestartSessionKey` is never cleared, so stale ownership survives in-process restarts and can reject a *different* session's future continuation.

Fixes #106138

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool-restart path and the config-watcher path are two deferral polls racing for one emission; only the hookless winner preserved queued continuations. The bounded fix makes the emission point honor the parked hooks regardless of who emits: the caller's `beforeEmit` (reload secrets preflight) runs first, then the parked-hook drain loop runs with its original replace/reject semantics — its tail re-read also captures hooks accepted (`emitHooksQueued: true`) while the caller's preparation awaited, so no async window remains before emission where a queued continuation could be dropped. Session ownership (`pendingRestartSessionKey`) now clears exactly when the slot is consumed on every emission attempt (previously leaked on hooked emissions, and — because container restarts are in-process — across gateway generations), every prepared hook set is rolled back via `afterEmitRejected` on non-emitted outcomes, and `afterEmitFailed` callbacks are error-isolated so one throwing hook set cannot skip another's cleanup. The empty-slot path stays await-free because mid-flight intent/deferral consumers observe hookless emission latency. Merging the two restart state machines was deliberately left out of scope — this restores the invariant `continuationQueued: true` ⇒ continuation survives, without touching reload-handler semantics.

Concurrent-emitter interleaving (two emissions racing mid-`beforeEmit`) was reviewed and is already impossible: every emission path goes through `emitPreparedGatewayRestart`, which synchronously takes the restart-signal admission fence (`beginGatewayRestartSignalAdmission` sets `restartSignalPending` with no await between admission entry and fence), and a concurrent attempt blocks in `tryBeginGatewayIndependentRootWorkAdmission`. This single-flight contract is now documented at `emitPreparedGatewayRestartUnderAdmission`.

## User Impact

Agent-initiated gateway restarts (`gateway` tool `action: "restart"` with `continuationMessage`) now reliably resume after the restart even when a restart-required config change (e.g. `browser.noSandbox`) armed the config watcher's own deferral in the same window — the exact "config set, then restart" sequence agents commonly run. No config, protocol, or tool-surface changes.

## Evidence

- Production trace (issue #106138): reload deferral won the emission (`all operations and replies completed; restarting gateway now`), no sentinel recovery/notice/continuation followed, while an earlier tool-side emission in the same session delivered its continuation correctly.
- New tests in `src/infra/infra-runtime.test.ts` (+4): hooked emission drains parked hooks and emits once via the caller's `emitRestart` with ownership cleared for the next session; hooks accepted while caller preparation awaits ride the same emission; parked hooks get `afterEmitRejected` on non-emitted outcomes; every `afterEmitFailed` runs even when an earlier one throws. Existing #86742 different-session rejection cases and mid-flight timing probes unchanged and green.
- Validation (Blacksmith Testbox, synced worktree on current `main`): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over `src/infra/infra-runtime.test.ts`, `restart.deferral-timeout`, `restart-suspension`, `restart-coordinator`, `restart-sentinel`, `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session-restart.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/update.test.ts` — all shards pass; `tsgo` core lane clean; core test-types lane has 0 non-`ui/` errors (the 2 `ui/app-sidebar.ts` errors reproduce identically on clean `main` with the diff stashed — pre-existing, unrelated).
- **Live A/B behavior proof** (real gateway, mock Telegram + mock LLM, real `gateway` tool call, config-watcher deferral winning the emission): after-fix run delivers exactly one sentinel recovery (`Gateway restart ok`) and exactly one continuation turn; before-fix run (`src/infra/restart.ts` reverted to `main`, rebuilt) loses both despite `continuationQueued: true`. Full logs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106174#issuecomment-4956370473
- Codex autoreview: clean, "patch is correct (0.88)", no actionable findings.
