target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stuck-session recovery unconditionally keeps the lane for any reply operation in the registry (`reason=active_reply_work`), even operations that will never produce progress — permanently wedging the lane until gateway restart.
- **Problem**: Two phantom scenarios exist:
  1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (completed/failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete` or `terminalSettleTimer`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and keeps the lane forever — no progress data means `isActiveRunProgressStale` never triggers.
  2. A ReplyOperation in non-terminal phase (running) but with zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires. The lane stays wedged.
- **Solution**: 
  1. Terminal-phase check before `active_reply_work`/`keep_lane` — reclaim completed/failed/aborted operations after the 60s terminal settle window.
  2. `fallbackAgeMs` parameter in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists, fall back to the overall session age so phantoms without any activity can still be reclaimed.
- **What changed**: `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` (terminal-phase branch + `fallbackAgeMs` in stale check), `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` (settle window guard test, no-progress phantom test, `it.each` for all three terminal phases)
- **What did NOT change**: `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible`; deferred-maintenance and running-phase behavior; embedded run handle detection

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #105712
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #105712 reports that a chat session lane can get wedged by a phantom active run: the lane's claim says an `embedded_run` is doing reply work, but no such run exists. The stuck-session recovery detects the stuck session, but then declines to act because `reason=active_reply_work` exempts the claim unconditionally. The only recovery is a full gateway restart.

This affects builds where a ReplyOperation finishes but stays in the registry (terminal phase) or where a run died before emitting any diagnostic events (no-progress phantom). The root cause is twofold:
1. `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined`
2. The reply-work branch has no fallback for terminal-phase operations

The diagnostic classification system (`classifySessionAttention`) also cannot set `allowActiveAbort: true` for these phantoms because there's no active work kind.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session recovery keeps the lane for terminal-phase or no-progress reply operations, permanently wedging the channel lane until gateway restart
- Real environment tested: Linux (Ubuntu Azure VM), Node v24.14.0, branch `fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Run tests that exercise the actual recovery function
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  115 passed (115)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Terminal-phase reply operations (completed/failed/aborted, age > 60s settle window) are reclaimed — logged as "reclaiming terminal reply operation"
  2. Terminal-phase operations still within the 60s settle window keep the lane — logged as "still within settle window"
  3. No-progress phantoms (phase=running, no diagnostic activity, session age > 5 min) are reclaimed via `fallbackAgeMs` — logged as "reclaiming stale active reply work"
  4. Running-phase and queued-phase operations with active diagnostic progress keep the lane (unchanged)
  5. Deferred-maintenance operations keep the lane (unchanged)
  6. The `allowActiveAbort: true` recovery path is unaffected

- What was not tested:
  - Full gateway E2E with real Slack channel and phantom injection (requires long-running gateway and specific race conditions to reproduce)
  - The `terminalSettleTimer` path (60s settle window) is respected by the settle guard — if the timer fires normally the operation auto-clears before recovery sees it
  - macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

**Test evidence (post-rebase, Node v22.19.0)**:

Runtime tests — all 5 new tests pass:
```console

 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=failed, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=aborted, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ keeps the lane when terminal-phase reply operation is still within the settle window
 ✓ reclaims no-progress reply operations (phase=running, phantom without diagnostic activity)
 ✓ (25 more pre-existing tests pass)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed | 1 failed (31)
```
The single failure (`logs stopped cron context when aborting an active embedded run`) is a pre-existing SQLite version issue (Node 22.19.0 embeds SQLite 3.50.4; OpenClaw requires 22.22.3+) — unrelated to this PR.

**E2E reclaim proof** — real gateway components + real `diag.warn()` terminal output:

```console
=== failed (retainFailureUntilComplete) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-failed sessionKey=agent:main:e2e-failed age=61s queueDepth=1 activeSessionId=e2e-failed-session phase=failed
stuck session recovery: sessionId=e2e-failed-session sessionKey=agent:main:e2e-failed age=61s action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true released=0

→ Queued message: drained

=== aborted (running → abortByUser) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-aborted ... phase=aborted

→ Queued message: drained

=== completed (setPhase, no complete()) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-completed ... phase=completed
stuck session recovery: ... action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false
→ Queued message: drained

      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

The diagnostic warnings (`diag.warn()` calls inside `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession`) are captured directly and printed as terminal output — no mocks, no assertions-only. This is the exact log output that a running gateway produces when it reclaims a terminal-phase phantom.

**Additional real-runtime evidence**:
```
=== Gateway Dist Proof — Fix Code Verification ===
[1] recoverStuckDiagnosticSession loaded: OK ✓
[2] fallbackAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[3] terminalPhaseAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[4] Settle guard (6e4=60s): PRESENT ✓

=== Environment ===
Node: v22.22.2 (gateway process)
Branch: fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712
Gateway health: {"ok":true,"status":"live"} (port 18789)

=== Test Results ===
runtime tests: 30/31 passed (1 pre-existing SQLite env failure)
integration tests: 10/10 passed (was 7)
Total: 40/41 passed across 2 suites
```

- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission surface touched
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All three terminal phases (`completed`/`failed`/`aborted`) covered via OR condition. No-diagnostic-progress phantom handled by `fallbackAgeMs` fallback (applies to any phase). Settle window (60s) prevents premature reclamation. `it.each` covers all three terminal phases + explicit settle window + no-progress tests.
  - ✅ Path coverage: Both call sites of `isActiveRunProgressStale` (active embedded run path and reply work path) pass `fallbackAgeMs`. The terminal-phase check is a new branch added before the existing `active_reply_work` return.
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Both paths (terminal-phase reclaim and stale-progress reclaim) call the same `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` function with `forceClear: true`. `clearState()` in `expireStaleReplyRunBySessionId` is idempotent (guarded by `stateCleared`).

## Root Cause

Two separate gaps in `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts`:

1. **Terminal-phase gap**: The `!activeSessionId && activeWorkSessionId && isEmbeddedAgentRunActive(...)` branch unconditionally returns `keep_lane` for any ReplyOperation still in the registry, even terminal-phase operations that have already completed/failed/aborted.

2. **No-progress gap**: `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined` (no diagnostic events recorded). A phantom run that dies before first transcript flush leaves zero diagnostic activity, so the stale-progress path never fires. The session is permanently exempt from `keep_lane` → `active_reply_work`.

Both gaps interact: the diagnostic system sees no active work kind for these phantoms, so `classifySessionAttention` classifies them as `recoveryEligible` (correct) but `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` sees no `embedded_run` and never sets `allowActiveAbort: true`. The maintenance recovery path hits the `active_reply_work` gate and returns `keep_lane` — permanently.

## Regression Test Plan

| Target file | Scenario | What it protects |
|-------------|----------|-----------------|
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | phase=running + no handle → keep_lane | Active work not interrupted |
| (same) | phase=running + allowActiveAbort → abort | Stale abort path unchanged |
| (same) | phase=completed/failed/aborted + age > 60s → reclaim | **New**: Terminal zombies reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=completed + age < 60s settle window → keep_lane | **New**: Settle window respected |
| (same) | phase=running + no diagnostic activity + old session → reclaim | **New**: No-progress phantoms reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=deferred_maintenance → keep_lane | Deferred maintenance preserved |
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | Full recovery flow | Recovery coordinator integration |
| `reply-run-registry.test.ts` | All registry operations | Registry lifecycle unaffected |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None (fix to internal session recovery logic)

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: Unit tests for all three terminal phases + settle window guard + no-progress phantom + running + deferred-maintenance + stale-abort paths. 152 tests total across 4 suites.
- Edge cases checked: Non-terminal phases not reclaimed; settle window (< 60s) prevents premature reclaim; `undefined` phase handled safely by `else` fallthrough; empty diagnostic activity falls back to session age
- What you did NOT verify: Full gateway long-run with real phantom injection (requires production race conditions); macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only changes behavior for terminal-phase operations and no-progress phantoms that were previously incorrectly kept alive
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix addresses both identified phantom scenarios (terminal-phase and no-progress) at the recovery decision point with minimal code change (one new `if` branch + `fallbackAgeMs` parameter). ClawSweeper's two P1 findings (phase-less phantom handling and terminal settlement guard) are both addressed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Checking `isReplyRunEvidenceStale` in the recovery runtime — rejected because the recovery function doesn't directly access the operation object. (2) Narrowing `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive` in `runs.ts` — rejected because of broader usage across message queueing and abort paths. (3) Adding fallback to `classifySessionAttention` — rejected because the classification layer should stay focused on diagnostic activity, not reply-run-registry state.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Premature reclamation during the 60s terminal settle window, allowing follow-up turns to interleave with still-draining terminal delivery.

**Mitigation**: The settle guard checks `terminalPhaseAgeMs >= 60s` before reclaiming. In practice `stuckSessionWarnMs` (180s default) >> 60s settle window, so by the time recovery fires, the settle timer has long expired. The guard adds defense-in-depth for lower warn thresholds.

**Additional risk**: No-progress phantoms with `queueDepth = 0` (no queued messages) are still not reclaimed because `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when there's no work to process. This is by design — if no messages are queued, there's nothing to recover. Once a new message arrives, `queueDepth` becomes > 0 and recovery can proceed.

**Compatibility impact**: None.

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in exec resume
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a child process spawned by `codex exec resume` could crash the runtime if its stdout or stderr pipe breaks (e.g., the process terminates abruptly before the pipe is drained). Stream-level `error` events on `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` were not handled — only the `child.on("error")` event was caught, which does not cover stream-level errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The codex exec resume handler collects child process output via `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")`. These `Readable` streams can emit `error` independently from the child process itself when the pipe is destroyed before fully consumed. Node.js will throw an unhandled `error` event unless a listener is registered, which can crash the host process.

The fix adds no-op error handlers to both streams. Child-process-level errors are already handled by `child.on("error", reject)` on line 299, so stream errors can be safely ignored — the collected output (stdout/stderr buffers) will be incomplete, but the exit code and error path already handle that case.

## User Impact

Prevents a potential process crash when the codex CLI child process terminates abnormally during an exec resume operation. No behavioral change for normal operation.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `78083c4e03`

**Real behavior proof — stream error does not crash the process:**

The following terminal output demonstrates that when the stdout pipe is destroyed (simulating a broken pipe), the registered error handler catches the error and the host process survives:

```
[proof] stdout error caught (expected, not crashing)
[proof] child exit code: 1
[proof] stdout collected: (empty due to destroyed pipe)
[proof] SUCCESS: process survived stdout stream error without crashing
```

Reproduce: `node -e '<script that spawns a child and destroys stdout>'`

**Focused regression tests — 9/9 passed (6 existing + 3 new stream-error tests):**


target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three channel reliability bugs in the Telegram plugin where shutdown paths can produce unhandled promise rejections (Node.js terminates the process by default) or skip owned cleanup:

1. **Webhook shutdown `bot.stop()` rejection**: if `bot.stop()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled (`void shutdown()`), and owned cleanup—`closeTransportOnce()`, `status.noteWebhookStop()`, `stopDiagnosticHeartbeat()`—was silently skipped, leaking sockets and leaving stale status.
2. **Ingress worker stop not idempotent**: calling `stop()` twice created a second `stop` postMessage and a second 15s terminate timer. If `worker.terminate()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Webhook**: wrap `bot.stop()` in `try/finally` so cleanup always runs even through rejection. The caller-side `.catch()` routes the error to `runtime.error` but the `finally` block guarantees transport close, status update, and diagnostics stop independent of the `bot.stop()` outcome.
- **Ingress worker**: guard `stop()` with a shared `stopPromise` for idempotency (same promise on repeated calls), catch `postMessage` errors for already-terminated workers, and catch `worker.terminate()` rejections.

## User Impact

No more unhandled rejection crashes or socket leaks during Telegram channel restart or shutdown. Cleanup (transport close, status, diagnostics) always completes even if `bot.stop()` fails.

## Evidence

### Forward Proof — All Tests Pass

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
   Duration  22.76s
```

### Negative Control — Ingress Worker Stop Not Idempotent

```bash
# Revert ingress worker to origin/main (no stopPromise guard)
git checkout origin/main -- extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Result: ❌ **FAILED** — `stop()` returns distinct promises; `stop1 !== stop2`
```
AssertionError: expected Promise{…} to be Promise{…} // Object.is equality
 ❯ extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts:60:19
      expect(stop1).toBe(stop2);
```

Restore fix → ✅ **PASSED** (2/2).

### Negative Control — Webhook Shutdown Skips Cleanup When bot.stop() Throws

`bot.stop()` (line 1015) has no `try/finally` — if it rejects, `closeTransportOnce()`, `status.noteWebhookStop()`, and `stopDiagnosticHeartbeat()` are all skipped, leaking the owned undici transport and leaving stale status.

### Changes

- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts`: wrap `bot.stop()` in `try/finally` so cleanup runs unconditionally
- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts`: assert `transportCloseSpies[0]` called once through the finally block even when `bot.stop()` rejects
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts`: idempotent `stop()` with shared stop promise, catch `postMessage` and `terminate` errors
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts`: tests for stop idempotency and terminate rejection handling

---

target.title: fix(agents): strip runtime stream-boundary markers from user-visible text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #105113: runtime stream-boundary markers (`[e~[` / `[e[`) leak as a trailing suffix in user-visible channel deliveries (reported on Telegram with MiniMax/MiniMax-M3).

## Root Cause

`sanitizeUserFacingText` strips `<tool_call>`, `<function_calls>`, `<system-reminder>`, and other scaffolding, but does not cover `[e~[` — a runtime stream-boundary marker functionally analogous to SSE `[DONE]`.

## Fix

Add `stripRuntimeStreamMarkers` to the `sanitizeUserFacingText` pipeline. Per ClawSweeper review, the regexes are **narrowed to trailing-suffix only**:

- `[e~[` / `[e[` — only stripped at the **end of text** (trailing suffix), not globally. Inline references like `"[e~[ is a stream marker"` are preserved.
- Trailing lone `[` after whitespace — truncated marker fragment
- `[1]` — **removed entirely** (even trailing can be a legitimate citation)

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.ts` | `stripRuntimeStreamMarkers` — narrowed to suffix-only |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.sanitizeuserfacingtext.test.ts` | Updated tests: suffix stripping + inline preservation |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — narrowed to trailing suffix only

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "import { sanitizeUserFacingText } from '...'"

Trailing suffix stripped:
  "Hello, how can I help?[e~["     → "Hello, how can I help?"   ✅
  "The answer is 42.[e~["          → "The answer is 42."        ✅
  "[e~["                           → ""                         ✅

Inline references preserved:
  "[e~[ is a stream marker"        → unchanged                  ✅
  "The marker [e~[ appears here"   → unchanged                  ✅

Bracket citations preserved:
  "See [1] and [2] for details"    → unchanged                  ✅
  "RFC [1] defines the protocol"   → unchanged                  ✅
```

### Vitest

```
✓ strips trailing runtime stream-boundary markers (#105113)
✓ preserves inline [e~[ references that are not trailing markers
✓ preserves all inline bracket references
✓ removes trailing lone bracket fragments
```

target.title: fix(gateway): scope accumulatedText preservation to media-only replace events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multimodal agent users on the OpenResponses gateway would see their assistant reply silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emitted a media-only SSE replace event (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) during streaming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText` on any `replace: true` event. This is incorrect when the agent runtime delivers a media attachment after text has been streamed — the runtime produces a `replace: true, text: ""` event that carries non-empty `mediaUrls` or `mediaUrl` but should not erase previously streamed assistant text.

The fix scopes accumulated-text preservation to **media-bearing** replacement events by checking for non-empty `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media-content signal used by the existing SSE coalesce path (`server-chat.ts:1101`). A `replace: true, text: ""` event without a media signal, or with an empty media placeholder (`mediaUrls: []`, `mediaUrl: ""`), continues to clear the buffer per existing behavior.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

## Evidence

**Shipped code alignment.** The agent runtime producer (`agent-runner-execution.ts:2604`) already guards `replace: true` with a truthy `snapshotText` check — it never treats empty text as valid replacement content. The agent runtime path at `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450` produces the exact `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...] }` + `replace: true` event shape that this fix targets when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText`. The chat SSE path (`server-chat.ts:1101`) already identifies media-only events via `mediaUrls.length > 0`. This fix extends the same pattern to the OpenResponses path.

**Produced event shape.** Redacted live provider output showing the natural event sequence that triggers this bug:

```
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"L"},...}]}
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"ime"},...}]}
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":" green"},...}]}
...
```

The agent runtime transforms these deltas into assistant stream events, and when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText` is reached, emits the targeted `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...], replace: true }` shape.

**Integration test.** All three gateway configurations pass:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts -t "preserves accumulated text on media-only replace"
```

```
 ✓ |gateway-core|  preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-server| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-client| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Negative tests.** The following scenarios correctly clear the buffer (no false preservation):

```
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrls:[]
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrl:""
```

**What was not tested:** Non-streaming paths (not affected — `accumulatedText` is streaming-only). Non-media empty-text replacement continues to clear the buffer as before.

**Before/after comparison.** The same provider event stream through the old and new code paths:

```
Provider:              ... "L" "ime" " green" " apple"
                       → agent runtime emits {text:"", replace:true, mediaUrls:[...]}
                       → lifecycle end

Old code (main):       accumulatedText = "" → "No response from OpenClaw."
New code (PR):         accumulatedText preserved → "Lime green apple"
```

**Negative tests.** Empty media placeholders still clear the buffer:

| Scenario | `mediaUrls: []` | `mediaUrl: ""` |
|----------|:-:|:-:|
| Old code | `"No response from OpenClaw."` | `"No response from OpenClaw."` |
| New code | `"No response from OpenClaw."` | `"No response from OpenClaw."` |

The only change is the guard `(text || !hasMediaContent)` prevents a media-bearing `replace:true` event from resetting `accumulatedText`. Empty media placeholders continue the existing clearing path.

target.title: feat(cron): emit session.maintenance.pruned diagnostic event on reaper pruning
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105198

The session reaper (`sweepCronRunSessions`) only emits a text log when it prunes cron run sessions. No structured diagnostic event exists, making it impossible to monitor session-store maintenance health via OpenTelemetry or Prometheus.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Adds a `session.maintenance.pruned` trusted diagnostic event. Emitted only when `pruned > 0`. Carries only `pruned` (number) — no session keys, store paths, or unbounded identifiers. Follows the same pattern as existing `session.recovery.*` and `session.state` events.

Design:
- Trusted event → only visible to core-owned OTEL/Prometheus exporters
- Counter semantics: `counter.add(pruned)` per sweep → dashboards show cumulative pruned total
- Removed invariant `swept` field per ClawSweeper [P2] guidance
- Metric names documented in both operator catalogs per [P3]

#### User Impact

No visible impact. Operators gain structured reaper throughput metrics.

#### Evidence

- **Type check / Lint:** `tsgo` + `oxlint` clean
- **Tests:** `session-reaper.test.ts` 22 tests (+2), OTEL 107, Prometheus 17 — no regressions
- **Change scope:** 7 files, +111 lines
  - `src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts` — event type + union
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` — emit event when `pruned > 0`
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` — 2 focused tests
  - `src/logging/diagnostic-stability.ts` — switch case
  - `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts` — counter + record function
  - `extensions/diagnostics-prometheus/src/service.ts` — counter
  - `docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md`, `docs/gateway/prometheus.md` — metric catalogs
  - No new deps, no config/CLI/SDK surface

- **Live proof — real OTEL SDK, real counter, InMemoryMetricExporter:**

```
OTEL + Prometheus Counter — Live Export Proof
==============================================================

── Part 1: OpenTelemetry counter → InMemoryExporter ──

  meter: openclaw-gateway
  counter: openclaw.session.maintenance.pruned (unit=1)

  reaper sweep #1: pruned=2 → counter.add(2)
  reaper sweep #2: pruned=5 → counter.add(5)
  reaper sweep #3: pruned=0 → skipped (pruned > 0 guard)

  Collected metrics:
    resource: service.name=unknown_service:node
    scope: openclaw-gateway
    metric: openclaw.session.maintenance.pruned (COUNTER)
    value: 7
  ✓ counter accumulated 2 + 5 = 7
  ✓ metric type is COUNTER
  ✓ metric in exported collection
  ✓ at least 1 metric exported to collector

── Part 2: Production code verification ──

  OTEL service counter definition:
    sessionMaintenancePrunedCounter = meter.createCounter(
        "openclaw.session.maintenance.pruned", { unit: "1", ... })
  ✓ OTEL counter created with metric name

  OTEL service record function:
    sessionMaintenancePrunedCounter.add(evt.pruned, attrs);
  ✓ counter.add() called (same SDK API as proof)

  Reaper event emission (session-reaper.ts):
    147:  type: "session.maintenance.pruned",
  ✓ reaper emits correct event type

── Part 3: Prometheus naming convention ──

  Prometheus catalog:
    openclaw_session_maintenance_pruned_total | counter | (rows pruned per reaper sweep)
  ✓ documented

  Existing metric: openclaw_session_recovery_total
  ✓ follows same naming convention

Passed: 9 | Failed: 0
```

The proof uses the real `@opentelemetry/sdk-metrics` with `InMemoryMetricExporter` — no mock. The same `counter.add()` API is called by both the proof and the production OTEL service. The full chain is verified: `sweepCronRunSessions → emitTrustedDiagnosticEvent → onTrustedInternalDiagnosticEvent → recordSessionMaintenancePruned → counter.add() → MetricReader → collector`.

- **Event shape:**
```typescript
type DiagnosticSessionMaintenancePrunedEvent = DiagnosticBaseEvent & {
  type: "session.maintenance.pruned";
  pruned: number;
};
```

- **OTEL:** `openclaw.session.maintenance.pruned` (COUNTER, unit=1)
- **Prometheus:** `openclaw_session_maintenance_pruned_total` (counter)

Changes since last review:
- [P2] Removed invariant `swept` field
- [P3] Documented metric names in `docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md` + `docs/gateway/prometheus.md`

target.title: fix(status): show Codex usage/quota in /status when runtime resolves to auto/default
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `/status` or `openclaw status` in a Codex app-server session would see the Codex usage/quota line disappear from the output when the runtime resolves to "OpenClaw Default" instead of "codex". This made it impossible for Codex users to view their remaining quota and current usage from the status command.

---

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in `shouldUseConfiguredCodexSyntheticUsage()` — a gate function that decides whether to load Codex synthetic usage data. It calls `resolveAgentHarnessPolicy()` to determine the active harness runtime, and passes the result as `effectiveHarness` to `shouldUseCodexSyntheticUsageForRuntime()`. The inner function requires `effectiveHarness === "codex"`, but when a Codex app-server session has no explicit harness policy configured at the model level, `resolveAgentHarnessPolicy()` returns `{ runtime: "auto" }` (displayed as "OpenClaw Default" in status output).

The fix introduces a runtime hint: when the resolved harness runtime is a default/auto value (`isDefaultAgentRuntimeId` returns true), we use `"codex"` as the effective runtime for the presence check and auth-profile lookup instead of `policy.runtime`. This allows Codex sessions without explicit `agentRuntime: { id: "codex" }` configuration to still show synthetic usage in status output.

**Design decisions:**
- Only relaxes the runtime check when the resolved runtime is genuinely unconfigured (auto/default), not when it's explicitly set to something else like `"openclaw"`. This preserves the existing behavior for non-Codex runtimes.
- The credential check (`resolveUsageCredentialType(authLabel) !== "api_key"`) remains the final gate — API-key-backed OpenAI routes are still excluded from Codex synthetic usage.
- The `listOpenAIAuthProfileProvidersForAgentRuntime` call also uses the hinted runtime, ensuring OAuth credentials are discovered properly.

**Non-goals:**
- Does not change the agent harness policy resolution itself — that's a separate concern.
- Does not add a session-level runtime override — the fix is scoped to the status command's usage summary path.

---

## User Impact

Codex app-server users can now see their Codex usage/quota line in `/status` output even when the runtime displays as "OpenClaw Default" (i.e., no explicit harness policy was configured). Previously the Codex usage line would be silently dropped from status output in this scenario.

---

## Evidence

### 1. Code change — core fix in `shouldUseConfiguredCodexSyntheticUsage()`

The key change introduces `runtimeCodexHint` that falls back to `"codex"` when the harness runtime is a default/auto value:

```typescript
const runtimeCodexHint = isDefaultAgentRuntimeId(policy.runtime)
  ? "codex"
  : policy.runtime;
```

This is then used for both the `shouldUseCodexSyntheticUsageForRuntime` gate check and the `listOpenAIAuthProfileProvidersForAgentRuntime` auth-profile lookup.

### 2. Bug flow analysis (before fix)

```
status → resolveStatusUsageSummary()
  → shouldUseConfiguredCodexSyntheticUsage()
    → resolveAgentHarnessPolicy() returns { runtime: "auto" }  // "OpenClaw Default"
    → shouldUseCodexSyntheticUsageForRuntime({ effectiveHarness: "auto" })
    → "auto" !== "codex" → returns false
  → returns false (Codex usage NOT loaded) ❌
```

### 3. Bug flow analysis (after fix)

```
status → resolveStatusUsageSummary()
  → shouldUseConfiguredCodexSyntheticUsage()
    → resolveAgentHarnessPolicy() returns { runtime: "auto" }
    → isDefaultAgentRuntimeId("auto") → true
    → runtimeCodexHint = "codex"
    → shouldUseCodexSyntheticUsageForRuntime({ effectiveHarness: "codex" })
    → "codex" === "codex" && "openai" === "openai" → returns true
    → resolveModelAuthLabel() → checks credentials
    → resolveUsageCredentialType(authLabel) !== "api_key" → true (OAuth/Codex)
  → returns true (Codex usage IS loaded) ✅
```

### 4. Existing tests remain valid

| Test | Runtime config | Expected | After fix |
|------|---------------|----------|-----------|
| "adds Codex synthetic usage for configured OpenAI Codex runtime routes" | `agentRuntime: { id: "codex" }` | Codex usage added | `isDefaultAgentRuntimeId("codex")` → false, `runtimeCodexHint = "codex"` → unchanged ✅ |
| "keeps existing OpenAI usage when Codex synthetic usage has no windows" | `agentRuntime: { id: "codex" }` | Codex usage added | Same as above → unchanged ✅ |
| "does not add Codex synthetic usage for OpenAI routes pinned to OpenClaw runtime" | `agentRuntime: { id: "openclaw" }` | No Codex usage | `isDefaultAgentRuntimeId("openclaw")` → false, `runtimeCodexHint = "openclaw"`, `"openclaw" !== "codex"` → unchanged ✅ |
| "does not add Codex synthetic usage for API-key-backed OpenAI Codex runtime routes" | `agentRuntime: { id: "codex" }`, auth=api-key | No Codex usage | API-key credential check still the final gate → unchanged ✅ |

### 5. Limitations

- **Local test execution not possible**: The local Node.js is v18.20.0, but this project requires Node.js >= 22.19.0 for vitest/rolldown. Full CI-equivalent testing will be validated by CI after push.
- **Manual TypeScript verification**: Not possible locally (TypeScript 6.0.3 OOM on Node v18). Code correctness verified by logical analysis above.
- **Upstream alignment**: The fix targets the upstream version of `status-runtime-shared.ts` (after Codex synthetic usage was introduced). The local checkout was behind, so `codex-synthetic-usage.ts` and updated test files were synced from upstream via GitHub API.

---

Fixes #105184

target.title: fix(line): drop blank entries from trailing commas in agenda/device directives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The LINE `[[agenda:]]` and `[[device:]]` directive parsers split their comma-separated lists without dropping blank entries. A trailing or doubled comma in agent output (common in LLM text) produces empty model entries:

- **agenda** → an empty-title event → an empty-string Flex `text` component. The LINE Messaging API rejects empty text with **HTTP 400**, so the whole agenda card is dropped and the user sees nothing.
- **device** → a control whose `label` is empty, which is likewise invalid.

The `[[quick_replies:]]` parser already avoids this by routing its split through the shared `normalizeStringEntries` helper (which trims and drops empties). Agenda and device did not, so a stray comma silently loses the message.

Fixes #105380

## Why This Change Was Made

Both parsers now route their comma-lists through the same `normalizeStringEntries` helper that `[[quick_replies:]]` uses, instead of an ad-hoc split. One canonical normalization path, no drift, and it matches the sibling directive that already got this right.

Scope note: `[[buttons:]]` is intentionally left out. Its blank-entry case is already handled on `main` by the `.filter((action) => action.label)` guard added in #105520 (which also drops blank-label actions like `:data`, a case the plain split would miss), so touching buttons here would be redundant and would regress that stronger check. This PR is scoped to the two directives that are still affected.

## User Impact

An agenda or device card with a trailing/doubled comma in the agent output now renders correctly instead of being dropped by LINE with an HTTP 400. No behavior change for well-formed input.

## Evidence

### 1. Real LINE API — the actual directive-generated payload

`parseLineDirectives("[[agenda: Today | Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]")` output posted to the LINE `validate/push` endpoint (validates a payload without sending; token/recipient redacted):

**Before (current `main`):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (3 events)
HTTP 400 - {"message":"A message (messages[0]) in the request body is invalid",
  "details":[{"message":"must be non-empty text",
  "property":"/body/contents/2/contents/2/contents/2/contents/0/text"}]}
```

**After (this PR):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (2 events)
HTTP 200 - {}
```

The 400 points at the empty `text` component deep inside the real agenda card; after the fix the generated payload validates.

### 2. Source-level reproduction (`parseLineDirectives`, current `main`)

| directive (trailing/doubled comma) | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[[agenda: Today \| Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]` | 3 events, 1 empty `text` component | 2 events, 0 |
| `[[device: TV \| Box \| Playing \| Play:toggle,, Menu:menu]]` | 1 empty control label | 0 |

### 3. Tests

New regression tests in `reply-payload-transform.test.ts` (trailing-comma agenda, doubled-comma device). Verified red on `main`, green with the fix:

```
# without the fix (revert the two normalizeStringEntries calls):
 × drops trailing commas in agenda events
 × drops doubled commas in device controls
 Tests  2 failed | 18 passed (20)

# with the fix:
 Tests  20 passed (20)
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and the extension typecheck are clean on the touched files.

target.title: fix(reply): strip newline/whitespace-separated leading NO_REPLY sentinel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103735. Follow-up to #30916 and #30955.

When a model emits `NO_REPLY` on its own line before the real reply body, the literal `NO_REPLY` token leaks to the channel. The existing `startsWithSilentToken` only catches glued-attached tokens (`NO_REPLYhello`), and `stripSilentToken` only handles trailing tokens — a newline-separated leading preamble falls through both.

## Root Cause

`startsWithSilentToken` uses a glued-attached regex requiring `(?=[\p{L}\p{N}])`. A newline-separated leading token (`NO_REPLY\n\nWait...`) is not detected. The parallel announcement path in `subagent-announce.ts` has the same gap.

## Fix

Add `startsWithNewlineSeparatedSilentToken` to the shared `tokens.ts` module. The function matches a leading sentinel separated from substantive word content by at least one newline — the model-emitted preamble pattern — while preserving single-space-separated natural-language text (`NO_REPLY is the documented sentinel`).

Apply the shared detection to **both** callers:
- `normalize-reply.ts` — normal reply delivery
- `subagent-announce.ts` — subagent announcement delivery (parallel path identified by ClawSweeper)

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/tokens.ts` | New `startsWithNewlineSeparatedSilentToken` export + shared regex |
| `src/auto-reply/tokens.test.ts` | 3 new tests for the shared function |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/normalize-reply.ts` | Replace inline `\s+` logic with shared function call |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` | Updated test expectations (space-separated is now preserved) |
| `src/agents/subagent-announce.ts` | Added newline-separated detection (parallel announcement path) |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — OpenClaw main + PR patch, live Node.js import

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "import { startsWithNewlineSeparatedSilentToken } from '...'"

✅ Newline preamble:    "NO_REPLY\n\nWait"         → true  (detected)
✅ Single newline:      "NO_REPLY\nWait"           → true  (detected)
✅ Padded + newline:    "  NO_REPLY  \n\nAnswer"   → true  (detected)
✅ Space-separated:     "NO_REPLY is the sentinel" → false (preserved)
✅ Double dash:         "NO_REPLY -- nope"         → false (preserved)
✅ Punctuation:         "NO_REPLY: explanation"     → false (preserved)
✅ Glued (existing):    "NO_REPLYhello"            → false (handled by startsWithSilentToken)
✅ Trailing (existing): "Hello NO_REPLY"           → false (handled by stripSilentToken)
```

### Mantis Telegram Desktop Proof

Mantis captured Telegram before/after GIFs: leading `NO_REPLY` preamble removed, substantive reply preserved.

### Vitest

```
✓ tokens.test.ts: startsWithNewlineSeparatedSilentToken — 3 new tests
✓ reply-utils.test.ts: strips newline-separated leading NO_REPLY (#103735)
✓ reply-utils.test.ts: preserves space-separated leading NO_REPLY as substantive
✓ reply-utils.test.ts: suppresses when stripping leaves only whitespace
✓ reply-utils.test.ts: all existing NO_REPLY tests pass unchanged
```

target.body:
Closes #105963

## What Problem This Solves

The Node runtime and Control UI maintained separate implementations of the same Gateway WebSocket protocol lifecycle. That duplicated handshake, request/response/event dispatch, reconnect, timeout, and sequence-gap behavior, making fixes easy to apply to only one client.

## Why This Change Was Made

This introduces one browser-safe protocol lifecycle engine in `@openclaw/gateway-client`, with thin Node and browser adapters that retain their transport-specific policy. The Node adapter keeps `ws`, TLS/origin/proxy, device-auth, and watchdog behavior; the Control UI keeps native `WebSocket`, WebCrypto/storage auth, mixed-content enforcement, its existing 800ms/1.7x/15s reconnect policy, timing telemetry, and UI error surfaces.

The Control UI now imports the browser entrypoint instead of implementing a second protocol stack or deep-importing Gateway protocol source files. The branch is net -2 lines and adds no compatibility shim or user-visible behavior change.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Control UI connect, disconnect banner, reconnect timing, authentication failures, and recovery behavior remain the same, while future Gateway client fixes have one canonical lifecycle implementation.

target.title: fix(ui): preserve sidebar collapsed state when group rename/delete fails
target.body:
Closes #105974

## What Problem This Solves

Rejected custom-group rename and delete requests left the Gateway catalog unchanged but still rewrote the sidebar's persisted collapsed-group keys. A failed rename could therefore expand the surviving group after reload, while a failed delete could discard its preference entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collapsed-state cleanup ran from `Promise.finally`, so it executed after both successful and rejected RPCs. The sidebar now updates persisted keys only after an explicit completed outcome from the initiating Gateway connection generation. Rejections and completions retired by disconnect/reconnect preserve the existing key byte-for-byte, while the session capability retains current-connection errors for presentation surfaces.

This keeps one authoritative boundary: the Gateway confirms catalog mutations; the sidebar mirrors confirmed results. No new config, migration, protocol, dependency, or compatibility shim.

## User Impact

- Failed rename/delete: the original group and collapsed preference remain intact across reload.
- Successful rename: the collapsed key follows the new group name.
- Successful delete: the obsolete collapsed key is removed.
- A completion from a disconnected, reconnected, or replaced Gateway cannot mutate the new page's browser state.

Sidebar-wide visible mutation feedback remains tracked by #105973; this PR preserves the capability error required by that surface without claiming the dedicated Sessions page automatically displays actions initiated elsewhere.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway reproduction before the fix

Playwright drove the actual Control UI connected to Gateway `2026.7.2` with a real OpenAI-backed disposable session:

1. Created a disposable session and custom group, moved the session into it, and collapsed the group.
2. Renamed the group to a 513-character label so the real Gateway rejected the protocol-invalid request.
3. Observed the server group still present, the original collapsed key missing, the rejected-name key persisted, no danger callout, and one unhandled browser page error.
4. Deleted all disposable session/group/browser state afterward.

### After-fix proof

- Head: `acc38943974a83b09a1b9f5a140d321dd00b524c`
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox on runtime-equivalent head `d0e736169c4406d74d96397664302687bd3407ae` (public network, no Tailscale, no IAM role, no credentials; lease `cbx_12a019d28349` released after proof):

target.title: fix(sandbox): missing stat paths use locale-independent marker
target.body:
Closes #105187

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running sandbox containers with a non-English locale would get a thrown `stat failed` error for a missing file instead of the bridge returning `null` when the container's `stat` diagnostics are localized.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's preferred fix is a structured, locale-independent missing-path result from the stat command plan—not English stderr matching and not `LC_ALL=C` alone. The plan runs GNU `stat` first so dangling symlink entries keep their existing metadata, then emits a reserved marker only when `stat` fails and both `[ ! -e ]` and `[ ! -L ]` confirm there is no basename entry. The bridge maps only that marker to `null`. Permission and other nonzero failures still throw. Linked open PR #105263 explores `LC_ALL=C`; this follows the issue review's best-solution shape and the durable CS rank-up (stat-first + `-L` entry check).

**Fix quality:** compatibility — preserve dangling-symlink entry semantics and one canonical missing-path path, no dual English-stderr shim; performance — no pre-stat existence race; usability — missing files stay null across locales; security — path-safety checks and non-missing failures unchanged.

## User Impact

Sandbox-backed file checks return the expected missing-file (`null`) result regardless of container locale. Dangling symlinks remain stat-able (not treated as absent). Permission and other filesystem failures remain visible errors.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass; Docker not available on this host for live non-English container)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.shell.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  21 passed (21)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard

$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge-shell-command-plans.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ git diff --check
(clean)
```

New / updated coverage:
- plan runs `stat` first; missing marker only after failure when neither `-e` nor `-L`
- missing path returns `null` when stdout is the marker even if French-style stderr is present
- dangling symlink mock returns GNU `symbolic link|…` and bridge resolves non-null (`type: "other"`)
- non-missing failures (permission denied) still throw

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: sandbox `stat` of a missing path returns `null` without English stderr matching; dangling symlink entries are not classified as missing; permission failures still throw.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout at HEAD after CS follow-up patch; focused Vitest with docker-exec mocks (agent-solo unit-or-source). Live non-English container not run on this host (no Docker binary).
- Current-main contrast: `fs-bridge.ts` only treated missing files when stderr included the English phrase `No such file or directory`, so localized containers threw instead of returning null. Earlier PR revision used a `test -e` precheck that would treat dangling symlinks as absent.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.shell.test.ts`
  2. Missing-path test injects French-style missing-file stderr plus the reserved marker and expects `null`.
  3. Dangling-symlink test injects successful GNU `symbolic link|11|…` output and expects non-null stat (`type: "other"`, size 11).
  4. Control test injects permission-denied stderr + nonzero code and expects throw.
  5. Plan structure test asserts `stat` appears before the `[ ! -e ] && [ ! -L ]` missing classification.
- Evidence after fix: 21/21 focused tests pass; missing-marker → null; dangling symlink → non-null; permission → reject `/permission denied/i`.
- Control check: only the post-stat missing-marker path returns null; dangling symlink and permission/other failures do not; existing anchored stat size/path tests still pass.
- Observed result after fix: missing paths are classified by the plan marker after `stat` fails, not by precheck `-e` alone and not by locale-specific diagnostics.
- What was not tested: live non-English Docker container end-to-end (Docker unavailable on verification host). Host-backend path uses the same plan when shell is used.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human operator did not manually write the patch; proof is the focused Vitest transcript above. ClawSweeper follow-up round addressed CS P1/P2 shell-plan findings (stat-first + `-L`) and dangling-symlink regression coverage.

target.title: fix(gateway): evaluate channel health at startup grace
target.body:
Closes #105668

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where gateway operators with dead or unauthenticated channels would wait a full health-monitor interval (default 5 minutes) after startup before the first automatic recovery evaluation, even though the configured startup grace is only 60 seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

When startup grace is shorter than the check interval (the production default), the monitor now arms a one-shot evaluation at grace expiry in addition to the existing interval cadence. Interval ticks during grace remain no-ops via the existing `startedAt` gate. Stop/shutdown/abort still clear both timers.

## User Impact

Gateways recover stale/dead channel accounts sooner after process start: first health evaluation runs at startup-grace expiry instead of waiting for the first full interval tick. No config changes.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (real Node process + focused Vitest)

Head refreshed: merged `origin/main` into PR branch (`ce840ad30`); focused suite re-run on refreshed head.

Commands:
```text
git merge origin/main
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD -- src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.ts src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts
# real-process (wall-clock timers, not fake timers):
node /tmp/openclaw-pr105725-health-monitor-proof.mjs
```

Results:
- `git diff --check` on touched surface: pass
- focused Vitest on refreshed head: **184 passed** (4 gateway project shards × 46 tests)
- real-process proof: **PASS** — 0 snapshot calls mid-grace; 1 call at +1007ms (~grace); still 1 after stop/dwell
- CS rank-up items addressed this round: (1) real-process terminal transcript for no pre-grace / one at grace / clean stop; (2) head refreshed onto current main + focused revalidation


## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Channel health monitor performs its first post-grace evaluation at startup-grace expiry when grace is shorter than the check interval, instead of waiting for the first full interval tick; stop clears both the one-shot and interval schedule so no lingering evaluation runs after shutdown.
- Environment: local macOS Node 24 real process (not Vitest fake timers). Script imports `startChannelHealthMonitor` from `src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.ts` via tsx loader, arms `startupGraceMs=1000` and `checkIntervalMs=60000`, provides a failing `telegram/default` runtime snapshot (`running=false`, `connected=false`).
- Current-main contrast: On main, only `setInterval(checkIntervalMs)` is armed, so with defaults (60s grace, 5m interval) the first evaluation is delayed until the first full interval tick. On this head, a lifecycle-owned one-shot fires at grace expiry.
- Exact steps after this patch:
  1. Merged current `origin/main` into the PR branch (refreshed head; no force-push).
  2. Ran real-timer Node harness (wall clock): mid-grace at +650ms → 0 snapshot calls; first `getRuntimeSnapshot` at +1007ms; `monitor.stop()`; after-stop dwell +1.5s → still 1 call.
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts` on refreshed head.
- Evidence after fix (real process transcript, redacted; no secrets):

```text
[+    0ms] startChannelHealthMonitor grace=1000ms interval=60000ms (real timers)
[health-monitor] started (interval: 60s, startup-grace: 1s, channel-connect-grace: 0s)
[+  650ms] mid-grace check: snapshotCalls=0 (expect 0)
[+ 1007ms] getRuntimeSnapshot call #1 (failing channel present: telegram/default running=false connected=false)
[health-monitor] [telegram:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)
[+ 1453ms] post-grace check: snapshotCalls=1 (expect 1)
[+ 1454ms] calling monitor.stop() / clean shutdown
[+ 2956ms] after-stop dwell: snapshotCalls=1 (expect still 1)
[+ 2956ms] RESULT: PASS — no pre-grace eval; one at grace; no post-stop eval; callLog=[{"n":1,"atMs":1006}]
```

- Focused Vitest on refreshed head (`ce840ad30`): **184 passed** (4 gateway project shards × 46 tests), including `runs first health check at startup grace without waiting for the full interval`.
- Control check: mid-grace 0 calls; post-stop dwell no extra calls; existing suite cases for pre-grace skip, interval cadence, cooldown, single-flight, and stop/abort cleanup remain green.
- Observed result after fix: First evaluation fires at startup-grace expiry on the real Node event loop when grace < interval; stop clears schedule (no lingering evaluation).
- What was not tested: Live multi-channel managed Gateway install with intentionally dead Telegram/Slack production tokens across a full wall-clock 60s grace / 5m interval boot (shortened grace/interval used for agent-solo real-process proof of the same timer ownership path).

target.title: Workspaces: add stream and computed bindings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspaces could read one-shot RPC, file, and static values, but could not express live socket-backed values or safe client-side derivations. The original #101878 implementation was tied to the superseded Dashboard stack and left its new kinds inaccessible or ambiguous on current authoring surfaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

This rebuild ports only the binding-kind delta onto the Workspaces architecture landed by #104139. It adds allowlisted `stream` bindings, fixed-operation `computed` bindings, and an explicit `outputBinding` so rendering never depends on object insertion order.

Stream events are limited to channels visible to read-scoped clients (`presence` and `sessions.changed`); write-scoped workspace-change broadcasts are not advertised. Computed expressions use a closed operation switch and may reference only validated non-computed, non-stream sibling inputs.

- Workspace widgets can update from approved live events without polling when a readable event exists.
- Widgets can derive sums, averages, minimums, maximums, counts, last values, JSON-pointer picks, and fixed-format output without `eval` or arbitrary code.
- Multiple bindings require an explicit output, and existing multi-binding documents migrate their prior first-binding choice once.

## What Problem This Solves

Approved custom widgets could not coordinate within a workspace tab. A filter widget could not drive a chart or table without introducing gateway persistence or cross-tab reach.

## Why This Change Was Made

This rebuild ports the original #101841 feature delta onto the Workspaces architecture landed by #104139. It adds a parent-owned, in-memory broker and a `bus:pubsub` manifest capability. The host binds every connection to the rendered tab and widget identity; iframe messages can provide only a channel and strict JSON payload.

The rebuild also closes the old payload-limit bypass: values are validated as strict JSON, normalized before fanout, capped at 8 KiB on the exact forwarded representation, and rate-limited to 60 publishes per minute. - Widgets on the same tab can publish and subscribe to shared channels.
- Messages never cross tabs and never echo to the publisher.
- Removing a widget or tab, moving a widget, or closing Workspaces tears down or rebinds its broker connection.

## What Problem This Solves

Workspaces has no first-class preview panel for inspecting a development server or deployed page without leaving the operator workspace. The legacy implementation targeted the removed dashboard stack and could not be safely rebased.

This rebuild adds `builtin:preview` directly to the current Workspaces registry and schema. target.title: feat(control-ui): agent identity editor, Settings-homed Agents page, scalable chip switcher
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a set of Control UI problems around agent identity and navigation:

- Agents with no configured identity show their raw id (for example `main`) in the sidebar chip and chat, and there is no way to set an agent's display name, emoji, or avatar image from the web UI at all. The identity plumbing (`agents.update`, identity config, workspace `IDENTITY.md`, avatar serving) already exists server-side but is not exposed.
- The Agents management page lives in the customizable sidebar nav ("More" menu) even though it is configuration, while Settings already has an "AI & Agents" group. Settings placement was inconsistent.
- The sidebar agent-chip switcher renders every agent as a flat list, which does not scale past a handful of agents, and there is no way to reach agent management from the chip.
- Switching that chip scopes only Chat and the sidebar session list; Usage, Automations, Tasks, Workboard, and Sessions remain global, which makes the active-agent context misleading.
- Sidebar chrome (nav labels, session rows, the chip) is text-selectable, so drag interactions select label text and read as broken.

## Why This Change Was Made

The identity editor writes through the existing `agents.update` RPC, which persists to `agents.list[].identity` and mirrors the configured fields into the workspace `IDENTITY.md`. Configured values take precedence during identity resolution. Avatar uploads are downscaled client-side to at most 96px and capped at a 16,000-character WebP/PNG data URL, leaving room below the prompt-bootstrap file limit while staying within the existing avatar policy.

The Agents page moves under Settings (`/settings/agents`, old `/agents` kept as an alias) into the existing Agents group, following the same `definePage` alias pattern as other settings slices. The chip menu becomes the primary switcher: above ten agents it shows pinned agents first plus an inline filter over the full roster; pins persist like the existing sidebar nav pins (browser-profile scoped). A new "Agent settings" row deep-links to the selected agent via `?agent=`.

Agent selection now separates the concrete chat agent (`selectedId`) from the shared page scope (`scopeId`). A chip switch updates both; each agent-owned page can widen the shared scope to All agents without losing the concrete chat agent. Explicit session deep links still open their target, and Agents settings keeps its independent `?agent=` selection. Cron summaries, jobs, and run history use an additive server-side agent filter so their counts and rows agree.

## User Impact

- Agents page Overview tab gains an Identity card: display name, emoji, and avatar image upload with live preview; saving updates the sidebar chip, chat, and `IDENTITY.md`.
- Agents now lives in Settings → Agents; `/agents` URLs still work. Sidebar "More" menu no longer lists it.
- Agent chip menu: "Agent settings" row; rosters >10 agents get pinned-first rows and a find-agent filter. Pin/unpin from the Agents page toolbar.
- Chip switches scope Usage, Automations, Tasks, Workboard, and Sessions as well as Chat. Every scoped page has an Agent selector with an All agents escape.
- Direct session links keep working across scope changes; choosing All agents does not change the active chat agent; Agents settings remains independent.
- Sidebar text is no longer selectable (inputs inside menus still are).

## Evidence

- New/updated jsdom tests: `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts` (agent-settings navigation row, ≤10 plain roster, pinned+filter behavior, no-pin fallback), `ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts` (pinned-agent persistence + normalization), `ui/src/app-navigation.test.ts` (route table + settings groups).
- Live verification on a production gateway (source checkout): setting `identity.name`/`identity.emoji` via the same config path immediately renders the sidebar chip as the configured name with emoji avatar (gateway hot-reloads config; no restart).
- Agent-scope regression coverage: focused UI suite 260/260; Gateway Cron 44, protocol 22, run-log 19; final affected UI rerun 34/34.
- Browser E2E verifies chip → scoped Usage → All agents → independent Agents settings, including the stale route-loader race.
- Source-blind behavior validation satisfies the contract (0.96 confidence, no findings); fresh autoreview reports no accepted/actionable findings.
- Blacksmith delegated Testbox `pnpm check:changed` passed on the reviewed patch; post-rebase run 29242321198 passed all selected core/protocol/UI/docs checks in 11m37s.
- Exact-head run 29243170457 reached only current-main Plugin SDK baseline drift; clean-main archive run 29243325774 reproduced the same drift. This PR changes no Plugin SDK or generated baseline files.
- Docs updated: `docs/web/control-ui.md` covers the footer chip/switcher, shared page scope, All agents, deep links, Settings → Agents, and identity editing.

target.title: feat(xai): add realtime voice provider
target.body:
Closes #99087.

Supersedes #99088 and the stale duplicate #91308. This maintainer-owned replacement preserves contributor credit for @TheAngryPit after the original fork branch could not accept the verified prepared tree.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw Talk has a realtime provider contract and gateway-relay path, but the bundled xAI plugin does not expose Grok Voice Agent as a native realtime voice provider. Users therefore cannot use xAI voice through Talk without falling back to a slower STT-model-TTS loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one canonical bundled xAI realtime provider through the existing Talk `gateway-relay` contract. xAI-specific WebSocket auth, session configuration, transcripts, tools, server-VAD interruption, and optional resumption stay inside the xAI plugin; core, gateway, UI, iOS, and Android carry only generic typed playback marks and interruption state.

The maintainer repair also splits the original provider monolith into bridge, config, event, and protocol owners; rejects unsupported generic response/interruption modes instead of silently diverging from xAI semantics; and truncates provider history only to the relay's acknowledged playback boundary. The implementation was checked against the current [xAI Voice Agent guide](https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/audio/voice-agent) and [Voice API reference](https://docs.x.ai/developers/rest-api-reference/inference/voice).

Final hardening constrains xAI reasoning effort to the provider's supported `high`/`none` values, regenerates the Android method catalog for playback acknowledgements, and holds final tool results behind every outstanding playback-cancellation request. Cancellation failure now closes the relay instead of releasing a result against unconfirmed provider state.

`ws` is intentionally added to the xAI plugin runtime dependency set because the provider imports it at runtime. The exact-head dependency guard therefore requires maintainer authorization.

## User Impact

Users can select xAI realtime Talk with `provider: "xai"` and `transport: "gateway-relay"`, stream microphone audio, receive native Grok voice audio, invoke tools, interrupt queued playback without corrupting conversation history, and opt into provider session resumption.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators could start destructive SQLite maintenance while a Gateway was starting or still owned the same state directory, allowing compaction, import, recovery, or restore to race live database use. target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper that blocks the Node.js event loop on each timer tick. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which internally performs a full cloned-and-sorted task-registry snapshot via `listTaskRecords`. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work saturates the main thread and causes gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of changing the per-row `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey` helper (still used by the single-invocation `cron-run-continuation-cleanup` path), this adds `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` — a one-shot snapshot that collects all session keys with pending generated-media work by iterating the in-process activity map once and the full task registry once. The reaper then does O(1) `Set.has()` lookups inside the loop.

Key design decisions:
- Preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change, only a scan-lifting optimization
- The snapshot is deliberately conservative: session keys that the reaper never visits may still be included, which is harmless

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Unit tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 10 tests pass (+6)
