target.title: feat(cloud-workers): openclaw worker mode running the embedded loop on the box
target.body:
Part of #104294 (cloud workers, milestone 2, PR 9 — the composition PR). Builds on the four landed milestone-2 backend contracts: #104688 (worker role), #104809 (transcript commits), #105275 (live events), #105719 (inference proxy). Design: `docs/plan/cloud-workers.md` (openclaw worker mode).

## What Problem This Solves

The four backend RPCs exist on the gateway side, but nothing yet runs an agent session ON a worker box. This PR adds `openclaw worker` mode: the entry point + worker-side runtime that dials the gateway over the reverse tunnel, admits with the minted credential + handshake, and runs the embedded agent loop on the box — with its persistence, model, and streaming seams tethered to the gateway, and tools running locally. This is where a worker box becomes capable of running a real session driven from the gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `openclaw worker` entry: restricted runtime (loadPlugins:"never", no channels, no gateway HTTP surfaces, throwaway mkdtemp 0700 state dir, in-memory empty auth storage — no local model auth profile read). Dials the tunnel-forwarded local socket, presents credential + handshake, attaches to its single assigned session. Fails closed on admission failure (with a bounded 120s admission deadline so a leased box can't burn forever on an unreachable gateway).
- Embedded runner rewired: session persistence -> transcript-commit RPC client (base-leaf CAS + runEpoch + seq, durable replay dedupe); model calls -> inference-proxy RPC client (provider/model reference strings only, streamed deltas + terminal, durable-replay resume); streaming -> live-event RPC client (monotonic seq, cumulative ACK, unacked-tail replay). Tools are the six coding tools (read/write/edit/apply_patch/exec/process), local-only, fail-closed availability check.
- Reconnect/resume: exact-frame transcript retry (ledger dedupe), cumulative live-ACK replay of the unacked tail, durable inference resume (single provider call, no double-bill). Owner-epoch supersession -> clean fenced exit. Oversized transcript messages fail closed producer-side.

## Deep-review fixes (a dedicated adversarial review found real concurrency/lifecycle bugs)

- **BLOCKER fixed:** stop() during an in-flight transcript commit spun forever (100% CPU hang on SIGINT/SIGTERM) because the terminal `stopped` state was indistinguishable from a transient interrupt and the commit retry loop treated it as retryable. Introduced a terminal WorkerConnectionStoppedError; retry loops now retry only transient interruptions and rethrow on any terminal state. Stop-in-flight and post-stop emit settle promptly.
- **Blast-radius fixed:** a gateway live-event window reset (a streaming-telemetry cursor reset) used to abort the entire run including a healthy in-flight inference turn. Now: satisfiable resyncs renumber the unacked tail from the gateway's expectedSeq (the gateway explicitly tolerates renumbered replay); an unrecoverable live-seam failure degrades to lossy preview streaming while inference/transcript continue. Live events are preview; they no longer kill the turn.
- **Dead-seam removed + contract documented:** the unused in-process resumeFromBase resync was removed (leaf-only rebasing is unsafe — an unseen transcript mutation means stale inference context). On stale-base-leaf the run fail-stops with an explicit lost-tail lifecycle error and no duplicate commit; relaunch-with-fresh-context is milestone-3 (placement) territory, now documented in docs/cli/worker.md.
- **Hardening:** the worker's session write path is now a real promise-chain mutex (was a pass-through relying on an unguarded serial-emission invariant); bounded admission deadline.

## User Impact

Opt-in only; dispatch/UI (target bar, placement) is milestone 3. This makes a worker box able to run a session end-to-end. No config/changelog/version-bump changes.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: src/worker (runtime, RPC clients, launch), gateway worker-environments, CLI command policy, lint-suppressions — 744 tests green, including the deep-review regression tests (stop-during-commit, resync-below-cursor renumber, live-seam-failure-does-not-abort, stale-base-leaf fail-stop, epoch-flip mid-inference, reconnect-mid-stream single provider call).
- Dedicated adversarial correctness review verified the hard parts correct (CAS/seq/replay dedupe, live ACK math, inference resume/no-double-bill, epoch fencing under withLock, restriction invariants) and found the bugs above, all fixed.
- Clean build (rm -rf dist): public plugin-SDK declaration graph 5,077,853/5,100,000; no [INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]. Type-aware lint, check:test-types, madge + import cycles zero, protocol:check, docs:map:check all green. Codex fresh autoreview clean.

target.title: fix(gateway): distinguish ENOENT from corrupt JSON in readManagedImageRecord
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readManagedImageRecord` used a bare `catch` that returned `null` for all errors, including `SyntaxError` from truncated or corrupt JSON metadata. This made it impossible to distinguish "attachment was never created" (ENOENT) from "attachment metadata was corrupted" (e.g. by a crash during write). Corrupted records were silently treated as non-existent, causing user-uploaded images to disappear without any diagnostic signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return `null` only for `ENOENT` (file not found) and propagate other errors (like `SyntaxError` from invalid JSON) so callers can respond appropriately. The HTTP handler now catches propagated errors and returns a 500 status instead of a misleading 404, making it possible to detect and diagnose metadata corruption.

## User Impact

Corrupted image metadata now results in a 500 error (visible in gateway logs) instead of silently returning 404 and making the attachment vanish. Valid "not found" scenarios continue to return 404 as before.

## Evidence

```text
$ npx vitest run src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

### Manual-run state contract

`cron run` is a debug/verification command. Manual runs record their outcome (lastRunAtMs, lastStatus, lastError) but do not advance scheduled state. - **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. Restoring the guard turns it green.
- **Fix**: Wrap the success/skipped `nextRunAtMs` recompute inside `if (opts?.isManual) { /* preserve */ } else { /* existing behavior */ }`, mirroring the already-guarded error branch. target.title: fix(config): clear snapshot marker on transient read error so future updates retry
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` marks a config path as snapshotted in a module-level `Set` before executing the read+write I/O. If the I/O throws a transient error (disk space, file locking), the catch block silently keeps the marker, permanently blocking all future snapshot attempts for that config path within the process lifetime.

**Solution**: Clear the snapshot marker in the catch block so a subsequent update can retry the snapshot.

**What changed**: 1 line in `src/config/backup-rotation.ts` — `preUpdateConfigSnapshotsWritten.delete(snapshotKey)` added to the catch block. Plus a test that simulates a transient read error and verifies retry succeeds.

**What did NOT change**: Successful snapshot behavior is unchanged (marker stays, preventing redundant writes). The "mark before I/O" strategy is preserved. No API, config, or public behavior changes.

Fixes #105431

## What Problem This Solves

The snapshot tracker marks a config file as snapshotted before the write operation succeeds. If a transient error occurs during snapshotting (e.g. disk space exhaustion or file locking), future updates are not snapshotted, leaving the system without a pre-update rollback point.

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: A transient I/O error during `createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` on a config path that hasn't been snapshotted yet.

**Root cause analysis**: Line 137 of `backup-rotation.ts` adds the config path to the module-level `preUpdateConfigSnapshotsWritten` Set. Lines 139-145 perform the actual readFile + writeFile inside a try/catch. Lines 146-148 catch any error but do nothing — the marker stays in the Set. All subsequent calls check `preUpdateConfigSnapshotsWritten.has(snapshotKey)` at line 133 and return early without retrying.

**Affected scope**: `src/config/backup-rotation.ts` — called by `update-cli/update-command.ts` once per config update. In-process only (the Set is not persisted).

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: A transient I/O error during config snapshot should not permanently prevent future snapshot attempts within the same process.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64, Node.js 22.x, OpenClaw main @ 16fa19cd72, real exported function driven directly (not mocked).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Drive `createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` directly: first with a `readFile` that throws EIO, then with a real fs to prove retry succeeds.
```bash
node --import tsx /tmp/proof-105431.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
=== L2 proof: createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot transient-error retry ===
Config path: /tmp/oc-105431-1d78031b/openclaw.yaml

Call 1 (readFile throws EIO): completed without throwing
  snapshot file exists: false

Call 2 (real fs after transient error):
  snapshot file exists: true
  content matches original? true

✅ PASS: transient error cleared marker → retry succeeded
   Without fix: Call 2 would be no-op (marker permanent).
```

**Observed result after the fix**: After a transient `readFile` error, the snapshot marker is cleared. A subsequent call with a working filesystem successfully creates the `.pre-update` snapshot with the correct content. Without the fix, the second call would return early because the marker was never cleared.

**What was not tested**: Concurrent process behavior (the module-level Set is inherently single-process). The fix does not change concurrent-safety properties.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

```
pnpm test -- src/config/config.backup-rotation.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
   Duration  16.03s
```

1 new test: transient read error → marker cleared → retry succeeds. All 8 existing tests pass unchanged.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — no API or config changes
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 8 existing tests pass
- [x] No breaking changes — successful-path behavior is identical (marker stays on success)
- [x] Mitigation: the fix is a single `Set.delete()` call in an already-existing catch block, adding no new code paths

target.title: fix(installer): validate upgraded Windows SQLite runtime
target.body:
Related: #106065

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows users upgrading Node through the installer could still be told that the newly installed runtime had an unsafe SQLite build, causing installation to stop even when the upgraded Node bundled a patched SQLite version.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer now resolves one concrete Node executable, reads its actual SQLite version, and validates that returned version in PowerShell. This avoids relying on child-process exit-code state across the package-manager upgrade boundary.

## User Impact

Windows fresh installs can continue after winget upgrades Node to a runtime with a patched SQLite build, while genuinely unsafe runtimes remain blocked.

target.title: fix(ai): avoid websocket cache clobber on stale reused release
target.body:
Closes #105434

## What Problem This Solves
Releasing a reused ChatGPT Responses WebSocket deleted `websocketSessionCache` by session id without checking whether a newer same-session connection already owned that slot. A stale release could close/evict a valid replacement connection.

## Why This Change Was Made
The new-connection release path already guarded deletion with an identity check (`cache.get(sessionId) === entry`). The reused-lease release path and idle-expiry callback did not, so a replacement-before-release race could clobber the newer socket. This extends the same ownership guard to those async teardown paths.

## User Impact
Cached WebSocket sessions are less likely to drop a healthy replacement connection when an older reused lease later releases or expires. No config or API changes.

## Evidence
- Source: `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` reused `release` + `scheduleSessionWebSocketExpiry` now delete only when the cache still references the captured entry (mirrors the existing new-connection release guard).

target.body:
# PR4/5 - inspection-first durable wake observability

## Context capsule

This PR is item 4 of the rebuilt beta3 durable core stack. After architecture/product review, PR4 is now intentionally inspection-first/read-only for public durable wake observability. Public durable wake write controls are deferred to PR5/later with lifecycle handoff proof.

## Durable core stack overview

- PR1/5 - docs/RFC/boundary anchor.
- PR2/5 - runtime foundation/core plus terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- PR3/5 - wake targets, durable producers, replay/resume semantics.
- PR4/5 - public durable wake inspection/observability plus CLI/Gateway/API read paths.
- PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff, final hardening, and any reviewed write-control contract.

## What Problem This Solves

PR3 persists durable wake obligations and delivery attempts. Operators and reviewers need a bounded public way to inspect those obligations without mutating persisted delivery/recovery state. This PR exposes read-only wake list, wake inspect, delivery-attempt list, unresolved obligations, and coordination projection paths while keeping write controls out of the public PR4 Gateway/CLI/protocol surface.

## Scope

- Public Gateway/CLI/protocol inspection paths:
  - `durable.coordination.get`
  - `durable.obligations.list`
  - `durable.wake.list`
  - `durable.wake.inspect`
  - `durable.wake.deliveryAttempts.list`
- Public durable wake write controls removed/deferred:
  - `durable.wake.acknowledge`
  - `durable.wake.supersede`
  - `durable.wake.mark`
  - CLI `wake-ack`, `wake-supersede`, `wake-mark`
- Generated Swift protocol models updated to remove deferred write params/result.
- Shipped plugin SDK compatibility preserved for `NodeSession` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime` with external packaged consumer proof.

## Non-scope

- No public durable wake mutation controls in PR4.
- No external transport delivery claim.
- No PR5 promotion.
- No cron changes.

## Architecture rationale

Public wake writes can terminalize persisted obligations and affect recovery/message delivery. PR4 keeps the public contract inspection-first so operators can diagnose durable state without creating compatibility expectations around write authorization, idempotency, terminal-state rejection, audit semantics, or lifecycle/session delivery handoff. Internal store write primitives remain available for PR5 integration but are not exposed as PR4 public API.

## Evidence

- Final head: `d7857aa47459c23e89fca642061b43010d5eeeb7`

target.title: fix(logging): warn when configured file writes fail
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using a configured log file could lose file logs without any diagnostic when appends failed. Blank persisted `logging.file` values were also accepted as canonical config even though they could never identify a writable file.

N/A (no existing issue)

## Why This Change Was Made

The logger now reports the first failed append in each uninterrupted failure episode and retries subsequent writes without flooding stderr. A successful append clears the warning latch; successful rotation does not, because rotation alone does not prove that writes recovered.

Blank values are repaired at the configuration owner boundary rather than by a permanent runtime fallback: `openclaw doctor --fix` removes an existing blank `logging.file`, and canonical validation rejects new blank values without trimming or otherwise transforming nonblank paths.

## User Impact

Operators now receive a concise stderr warning when the configured log file cannot be written. Once the path becomes writable, logging recovers without a restart; a later independent failure is reported again. Existing blank values have a doctor migration to the default log path, while valid configured paths keep their exact bytes.

## Evidence

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Failed file appends were swallowed and the returned failure signal was ignored, so OpenClaw could continue running while silently losing file logs. Blank persisted paths also remained malformed canonical configuration.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.14, branch `fix/logging-silent-file-write-failure`, head `56599e3457ff38c6683b52224757ae9974ccfe1a` rebased onto `upstream/main` `ffff72c43aedf5bdeb32a6836f577850207f8573`.
- **Exact steps or command run:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-logging-file-failure.mjs`
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of the `node` runtime verification (copied live output):

  ```text
  schema blank rejected=true; doctor removed=true; migrated valid=true
  consecutive failure warnings=1
  recovery append=true; exact path exists=true
  warnings after recovery and new failure=2
  ALL PASS
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Canonical validation rejects blank paths; doctor removes a shipped blank value while preserving sibling logging settings; two consecutive append failures emit one warning; a successful append recovers logging; and a later failure emits a new warning.
- **What was not tested:** A packaged OpenClaw deployment on a read-only container filesystem. The append-failure contract was exercised deterministically by placing a directory at the configured file path, then removing it to prove recovery on the same logger instance.

target.title: fix(slack): bound userCache growth with pruneMapToMaxSize
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from `users.info` API calls but has no pruning — every unique user ID accumulates forever. On a busy Slack workspace with thousands of users, this Map grows without bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

`channelCache` already uses `pruneMapToMaxSize(channelCache, 1024)` but `userCache` was missed. The fix adds the same pattern at 2048 entries.

## User Impact

- Prevents unbounded memory growth in long-running Slack monitor sessions
- Oldest entries are evicted when the cap is reached
- No behavioral change for typical usage (2048 entries covers most workspaces)

## Evidence

### 1. Before vs After — pruneMapToMaxSize Behavior (code-level proof)

```
================================================================================
 SLACK USER CACHE PROOF — PR #105978
 PID: 433977   Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C   Time: 2026-07-13T07:52:29.364Z
================================================================================

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  BEFORE: No pruning — cache grows without bound          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
  Insert 5000 entries, NO pruneMapToMaxSize
  Map size: 5000
  ✅ Map size === 5000 (unbounded)
  ✅ Key U000000 exists (oldest kept)
  ✅ Key U004999 exists (newest kept)
  → Memory leak: all 5000 entries retained forever

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  AFTER:  pruneMapToMaxSize(map, 2048) — bounded growth    ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
  Insert 5000 entries WITH pruneMapToMaxSize(map, 2048) after each set
  Map size: 2048
  ✅ Map size === 2048 (bounded)
  ✅ Oldest key U000000 evicted
  ✅ Key U002952 exists (newest kept)
  ✅ Key U004999 exists (newest kept)
  → Memory safe: only newest 2048 entries retained

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  EVICTION CHAIN: oldest N evicted when exceeding cap      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
  Insert 2050 entries → max 2048
  ✅ Size = 2048
  ✅ Oldest 2 keys evicted
  ✅ Newest 2 keys present
  → Insertion-ordered, oldest removed first

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  BELOW CAP: ≤2048 entries → no eviction                  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
  Insert 2048 entries (exactly at cap)
  ✅ Size = 2048
  ✅ All keys retained → no eviction within cap

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  EDGE CASES: NaN, Infinity, zero cap                     ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
  ✅ NaN cap → no-op
  ✅ Infinity cap → no-op
  ✅ Zero cap → clear
  ✅ Negative cap → clear

── Scenario Matrix ──
  Scenario                  Before (no prune)     After (cap=2048)
  ≤2048 entries             2048 kept             2048 kept ✅
  >2048 entries (5000)      5000 kept (∞)         2048 kept ✅
  Oldest re-request         cache hit (stale)     cache miss ✅
  NaN / Infinity cap        N/A                   no-op ✅
  Zero / negative cap       N/A                   clear ✅

 ALL PROOF PASSED ✅
```

### 2. Real Slack API — auth.test (valid bot token)

```
$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer \$SLACK_TOKEN" https://slack.com/api/auth.test
{
```

target.title: fix(ui): keep Worktree mutation errors visible
target.body:
Closes #106158

## What Problem This Solves

Worktree create, restore, delete, force-delete, and garbage-collection failures vanished from the Control UI before users could read them. Each mutation stored its error and then immediately ran `worktrees.list`; that refresh cleared the shared error state before rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

Post-mutation reconciliation now preserves the mutation error while a successful list refresh updates the rows. A list refresh failure still replaces the earlier mutation error because the page can no longer claim its displayed state is current. Ordinary page loads and connection-driven refreshes keep their existing clear-at-start behavior.

This keeps the contract at the Worktrees page owner boundary and applies uniformly to every mutation finalizer rather than special-casing restore.

## User Impact

When a Worktree operation fails, the actionable Gateway error remains visible after the automatic row refresh. The user can retry from the up-to-date table. If reconciliation itself fails, the page shows that newer list error instead.

## Evidence

- Real authenticated Gateway + Playwright reproduction on current `main`: created and deleted a disposable Worktree, made its source repository unavailable, clicked Restore, observed the Gateway rejection and successful follow-up `worktrees.list`, then confirmed `.callout.danger` count remained zero. Restored the source and fully removed the disposable Gateway registry/snapshot state afterward.

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stuck-session recovery unconditionally keeps the lane for any reply operation in the registry (`reason=active_reply_work`), even operations that will never produce progress — permanently wedging the lane until gateway restart.
- **Problem**: Two phantom scenarios exist:
  1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (completed/failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete` or `terminalSettleTimer`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and keeps the lane forever — no progress data means `isActiveRunProgressStale` never triggers.
  2. A ReplyOperation in non-terminal phase (running) but with zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires. The lane stays wedged.
- **Solution**: 
  1. Terminal-phase check before `active_reply_work`/`keep_lane` — reclaim completed/failed/aborted operations after the 60s terminal settle window.
  2. `fallbackAgeMs` parameter in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists, fall back to the overall session age so phantoms without any activity can still be reclaimed.
- **What changed**: `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` (terminal-phase branch + `fallbackAgeMs` in stale check), `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` (settle window guard test, no-progress phantom test, `it.each` for all three terminal phases)
- **What did NOT change**: `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible`; deferred-maintenance and running-phase behavior; embedded run handle detection

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #105712
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #105712 reports that a chat session lane can get wedged by a phantom active run: the lane's claim says an `embedded_run` is doing reply work, but no such run exists. The stuck-session recovery detects the stuck session, but then declines to act because `reason=active_reply_work` exempts the claim unconditionally. The only recovery is a full gateway restart.

This affects builds where a ReplyOperation finishes but stays in the registry (terminal phase) or where a run died before emitting any diagnostic events (no-progress phantom). The root cause is twofold:
1. `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined`
2. The reply-work branch has no fallback for terminal-phase operations

The diagnostic classification system (`classifySessionAttention`) also cannot set `allowActiveAbort: true` for these phantoms because there's no active work kind.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session recovery keeps the lane for terminal-phase or no-progress reply operations, permanently wedging the channel lane until gateway restart
- Real environment tested: Linux (Ubuntu Azure VM), Node v24.14.0, branch `fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Run tests that exercise the actual recovery function
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  115 passed (115)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Terminal-phase reply operations (completed/failed/aborted, age > 60s settle window) are reclaimed — logged as "reclaiming terminal reply operation"
  2. Terminal-phase operations still within the 60s settle window keep the lane — logged as "still within settle window"
  3. No-progress phantoms (phase=running, no diagnostic activity, session age > 5 min) are reclaimed via `fallbackAgeMs` — logged as "reclaiming stale active reply work"
  4. Running-phase and queued-phase operations with active diagnostic progress keep the lane (unchanged)
  5. Deferred-maintenance operations keep the lane (unchanged)
  6. The `allowActiveAbort: true` recovery path is unaffected

- What was not tested:
  - Full gateway E2E with real Slack channel and phantom injection (requires long-running gateway and specific race conditions to reproduce)
  - The `terminalSettleTimer` path (60s settle window) is respected by the settle guard — if the timer fires normally the operation auto-clears before recovery sees it
  - macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

**Test evidence (post-rebase, Node v22.19.0)**:

Runtime tests — all 5 new tests pass:
```console
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=completed, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=failed, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=aborted, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ keeps the lane when terminal-phase reply operation is still within the settle window
 ✓ reclaims no-progress reply operations (phase=running, phantom without diagnostic activity)
 ✓ (25 more pre-existing tests pass)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed | 1 failed (31)
```
The single failure (`logs stopped cron context when aborting an active embedded run`) is a pre-existing SQLite version issue (Node 22.19.0 embeds SQLite 3.50.4; OpenClaw requires 22.22.3+) — unrelated to this PR.

**E2E reclaim proof** — real gateway components + real `diag.warn()` terminal output:

```console
=== failed (retainFailureUntilComplete) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-failed sessionKey=agent:main:e2e-failed age=61s queueDepth=1 activeSessionId=e2e-failed-session phase=failed
stuck session recovery: sessionId=e2e-failed-session sessionKey=agent:main:e2e-failed age=61s action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true released=0
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted action=abort_embedded_run ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=0
→ Queued message: drained

=== aborted (running → abortByUser) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-aborted ... phase=aborted
stuck session recovery: ... action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false
→ Queued message: drained

=== completed (setPhase, no complete()) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-completed ... phase=completed
stuck session recovery: ... action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false
→ Queued message: drained

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

The diagnostic warnings (`diag.warn()` calls inside `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession`) are captured directly and printed as terminal output — no mocks, no assertions-only. This is the exact log output that a running gateway produces when it reclaims a terminal-phase phantom.

**Additional real-runtime evidence**:
```
=== Gateway Dist Proof — Fix Code Verification ===
[1] recoverStuckDiagnosticSession loaded: OK ✓
[2] fallbackAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[3] terminalPhaseAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[4] Settle guard (6e4=60s): PRESENT ✓

=== Environment ===
Node: v22.22.2 (gateway process)
Branch: fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712
Gateway health: {"ok":true,"status":"live"} (port 18789)

=== Test Results ===
runtime tests: 30/31 passed (1 pre-existing SQLite env failure)
integration tests: 10/10 passed (was 7)
Total: 40/41 passed across 2 suites
```

- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission surface touched
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All three terminal phases (`completed`/`failed`/`aborted`) covered via OR condition. No-diagnostic-progress phantom handled by `fallbackAgeMs` fallback (applies to any phase). Settle window (60s) prevents premature reclamation. `it.each` covers all three terminal phases + explicit settle window + no-progress tests.
  - ✅ Path coverage: Both call sites of `isActiveRunProgressStale` (active embedded run path and reply work path) pass `fallbackAgeMs`. The terminal-phase check is a new branch added before the existing `active_reply_work` return.
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Both paths (terminal-phase reclaim and stale-progress reclaim) call the same `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` function with `forceClear: true`. `clearState()` in `expireStaleReplyRunBySessionId` is idempotent (guarded by `stateCleared`).

## Root Cause

Two separate gaps in `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts`:

1. **Terminal-phase gap**: The `!activeSessionId && activeWorkSessionId && isEmbeddedAgentRunActive(...)` branch unconditionally returns `keep_lane` for any ReplyOperation still in the registry, even terminal-phase operations that have already completed/failed/aborted.

2. **No-progress gap**: `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined` (no diagnostic events recorded). A phantom run that dies before first transcript flush leaves zero diagnostic activity, so the stale-progress path never fires. The session is permanently exempt from `keep_lane` → `active_reply_work`.

Both gaps interact: the diagnostic system sees no active work kind for these phantoms, so `classifySessionAttention` classifies them as `recoveryEligible` (correct) but `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` sees no `embedded_run` and never sets `allowActiveAbort: true`. The maintenance recovery path hits the `active_reply_work` gate and returns `keep_lane` — permanently.

## Regression Test Plan

| Target file | Scenario | What it protects |
|-------------|----------|-----------------|
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | phase=running + no handle → keep_lane | Active work not interrupted |
| (same) | phase=running + allowActiveAbort → abort | Stale abort path unchanged |
| (same) | phase=completed/failed/aborted + age > 60s → reclaim | **New**: Terminal zombies reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=completed + age < 60s settle window → keep_lane | **New**: Settle window respected |
| (same) | phase=running + no diagnostic activity + old session → reclaim | **New**: No-progress phantoms reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=deferred_maintenance → keep_lane | Deferred maintenance preserved |
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | Full recovery flow | Recovery coordinator integration |
| `reply-run-registry.test.ts` | All registry operations | Registry lifecycle unaffected |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None (fix to internal session recovery logic)

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: Unit tests for all three terminal phases + settle window guard + no-progress phantom + running + deferred-maintenance + stale-abort paths. 152 tests total across 4 suites.
- Edge cases checked: Non-terminal phases not reclaimed; settle window (< 60s) prevents premature reclaim; `undefined` phase handled safely by `else` fallthrough; empty diagnostic activity falls back to session age
- What you did NOT verify: Full gateway long-run with real phantom injection (requires production race conditions); macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only changes behavior for terminal-phase operations and no-progress phantoms that were previously incorrectly kept alive
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix addresses both identified phantom scenarios (terminal-phase and no-progress) at the recovery decision point with minimal code change (one new `if` branch + `fallbackAgeMs` parameter). ClawSweeper's two P1 findings (phase-less phantom handling and terminal settlement guard) are both addressed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Checking `isReplyRunEvidenceStale` in the recovery runtime — rejected because the recovery function doesn't directly access the operation object. (2) Narrowing `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive` in `runs.ts` — rejected because of broader usage across message queueing and abort paths. (3) Adding fallback to `classifySessionAttention` — rejected because the classification layer should stay focused on diagnostic activity, not reply-run-registry state.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Premature reclamation during the 60s terminal settle window, allowing follow-up turns to interleave with still-draining terminal delivery.

**Mitigation**: The settle guard checks `terminalPhaseAgeMs >= 60s` before reclaiming. In practice `stuckSessionWarnMs` (180s default) >> 60s settle window, so by the time recovery fires, the settle timer has long expired. The guard adds defense-in-depth for lower warn thresholds.

**Additional risk**: No-progress phantoms with `queueDepth = 0` (no queued messages) are still not reclaimed because `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when there's no work to process. This is by design — if no messages are queued, there's nothing to recover. Once a new message arrives, `queueDepth` becomes > 0 and recovery can proceed.

**Compatibility impact**: None.

target.title: fix(ai): serialize ChatGPT websocket message decode order
target.body:
Closes #105435

## What Problem This Solves
`parseWebSocket` started an independent async decode task per `message` event. Blob-like frames await `arrayBuffer()` while strings decode immediately, so later frames could enter the parser queue first and reorder Responses stream events.

## Why This Change Was Made
Serialize decode-and-parse on a per-socket promise chain so arrival order is preserved without dropping the accepted binary/Blob path. Codex sibling `responses_websocket.rs` already consumes one WebSocket message at a time before reading the next; OpenClaw now matches that ordering invariant while keeping Blob compatibility.

## User Impact
ChatGPT Responses websocket streams no longer reorder events when a delayed Blob decode races a later text frame. Normal string-only traffic behavior is unchanged aside from the ordered chain.

## Evidence
- Codex contract checked: `../codex/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs:686-808` (sequential `ws_stream.next()`, binary rejected as unexpected).

target.title: fix(acp): preserve structured exec approval metadata
target.body:
## Summary

- Back ACP structured exec approval metadata with the real Gateway request contract and public `exec` caller.
- Preserve the originating approval title and `toolCallId` across Gateway-host, Node-host, pending approval, broadcast, and ACP `request_permission` boundaries.
- Correlate structured approvals by `sessionKey + toolCallId` when multiple ACP prompts share one session key.
- Rebase onto current `main`, preserve current abort handling, and keep generated Swift optional initializer parameters source-compatible with default `nil` values.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause fix at the public exec approval contract and ACP correlation invariant.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — the final rebased HEAD crossed the real Gateway, live-model, ACP permission, and command-completion boundaries; the focused regression, formatting, protocol generation, and diff checks passed.
- **Patch quality notes:** The 19-file diff is the smallest complete canonical chain because caller, schema, pending record, broadcast, parser, translator, generated protocol model, and their focused tests must agree; splitting it would recreate a parser-only or producer-only contract. The test-only `.catch(reject)` surfaces asynchronous harness failures rather than swallowing production errors. The translator's `return undefined` is the intentional ambiguity guard: duplicate matches must not bind an approval to the wrong prompt. A related open PR scan found no competing same-contract or canonical PR for this metadata and correlation gap.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The original parser read `request.title` and `request.toolCallId`, but the canonical producer path could not emit them because public `exec` callers omitted the metadata and the closed Gateway request schema did not accept, store, or broadcast it. After that contract was connected, structured `exec.approval.requested` events still lacked `runId`; with two active ACP prompts sharing one `sessionKey`, the translator used session-only uniqueness and dropped an event even when `toolCallId` uniquely identified the pending tool call.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The change repairs both source-of-truth invariants instead of masking a missing permission request downstream: metadata now originates at the real public exec caller and survives the Gateway contract, while the translator selects the active pending prompt by the correlation identifier already carried by that contract. Unmatched or duplicate ids still fail closed and retain the existing unique-session behavior.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** ACP clients can display the intended exec approval title and correlate the permission request with the original tool call instead of falling back to synthetic values. Concurrent ACP prompts sharing a Gateway session no longer lose an early structured approval solely because session-only matching is ambiguous.

Approval decisions, allowed options, command hydration, and fallback behavior for events without metadata remain unchanged.

## Origin / follow-up

- Follows #79337, which introduced ACP exec approval permission relay support.
- #3257 is related approval visibility context, but this focused Gateway-to-ACP contract fix does not claim to close it.
- No open competing PR was found for this structured exec approval metadata and correlation gap.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A real public `exec` tool call must carry its display title and tool-call correlation id through `exec.approval.requested` into ACP `session/request_permission`. If two ACP prompts share a session key, a structured event with a matching `toolCallId` must reach the correct ACP session instead of being dropped as ambiguous.

Closes #106170

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users selecting GitHub Copilot models could receive a `network connection error` after runtime token exchange, before the model request reached GitHub.

The same path could use synthetic 128K model limits instead of the selected account's live catalog limits, and could retain another profile's limits during profile rotation, direct-auth fallback, or compaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The complete fix keeps runtime credentials refreshable while ensuring OpenClaw selects its managed provider transport whenever exchanged auth is available. GitHub Copilot live catalogs and cached exchanged tokens are scoped to the source credential/profile, and normal plus compaction paths rematerialize model metadata whenever the active credential changes.

Cross-provider compaction only reuses a forwarded profile when its prepared auth plan matches the target provider/model. Route-less profile handling is gated by the provider's existing `preferRuntimeResolvedModel` ownership hook, so unrelated Claude CLI/PI auth overlays retain their current behavior.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(gateway): drain parked restart emit hooks on hooked emissions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`gateway` tool restarts queue a continuation (restart sentinel written in an emit hook, recovered on boot as a resume turn). When a config-reload restart deferral (`server-reload-handlers.ts` → `deferGatewayRestartUntilIdle` with its own `emitHooks`) wins the emission race, `emitPreparedGatewayRestartUnderAdmission` runs only the caller's hooks and never drains the parked `pendingRestartEmitHooks` — the sentinel is never written, so the promised continuation silently disappears and the session stays dead until a human pings it. Observed in production (see issue): the agent reported `continuationQueued: true`, told the user the task would "resume automatically after restart", restarted, and never resumed. Two follow-on leaks on the same path: the orphaned hooks' `afterEmitRejected` never fires, and `pendingRestartSessionKey` is never cleared, so stale ownership survives in-process restarts and can reject a *different* session's future continuation.

Fixes #106138

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool-restart path and the config-watcher path are two deferral polls racing for one emission; only the hookless winner preserved queued continuations. The bounded fix makes the emission point honor the parked hooks regardless of who emits: the caller's `beforeEmit` (reload secrets preflight) runs first, then the parked-hook drain loop runs with its original replace/reject semantics — its tail re-read also captures hooks accepted (`emitHooksQueued: true`) while the caller's preparation awaited, so no async window remains before emission where a queued continuation could be dropped. Session ownership (`pendingRestartSessionKey`) now clears exactly when the slot is consumed on every emission attempt (previously leaked on hooked emissions, and — because container restarts are in-process — across gateway generations), every prepared hook set is rolled back via `afterEmitRejected` on non-emitted outcomes, and `afterEmitFailed` callbacks are error-isolated so one throwing hook set cannot skip another's cleanup. The empty-slot path stays await-free because mid-flight intent/deferral consumers observe hookless emission latency. Merging the two restart state machines was deliberately left out of scope — this restores the invariant `continuationQueued: true` ⇒ continuation survives, without touching reload-handler semantics.

Concurrent-emitter interleaving (two emissions racing mid-`beforeEmit`) was reviewed and is already impossible: every emission path goes through `emitPreparedGatewayRestart`, which synchronously takes the restart-signal admission fence (`beginGatewayRestartSignalAdmission` sets `restartSignalPending` with no await between admission entry and fence), and a concurrent attempt blocks in `tryBeginGatewayIndependentRootWorkAdmission`. This single-flight contract is now documented at `emitPreparedGatewayRestartUnderAdmission`.

## User Impact

Agent-initiated gateway restarts (`gateway` tool `action: "restart"` with `continuationMessage`) now reliably resume after the restart even when a restart-required config change (e.g. `browser.noSandbox`) armed the config watcher's own deferral in the same window — the exact "config set, then restart" sequence agents commonly run. No config, protocol, or tool-surface changes.

## Evidence

- Production trace (issue #106138): reload deferral won the emission (`all operations and replies completed; restarting gateway now`), no sentinel recovery/notice/continuation followed, while an earlier tool-side emission in the same session delivered its continuation correctly.
- New tests in `src/infra/infra-runtime.test.ts` (+4): hooked emission drains parked hooks and emits once via the caller's `emitRestart` with ownership cleared for the next session; hooks accepted while caller preparation awaits ride the same emission; parked hooks get `afterEmitRejected` on non-emitted outcomes; every `afterEmitFailed` runs even when an earlier one throws. Existing #86742 different-session rejection cases and mid-flight timing probes unchanged and green.
- Validation (Blacksmith Testbox, synced worktree on current `main`): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over `src/infra/infra-runtime.test.ts`, `restart.deferral-timeout`, `restart-suspension`, `restart-coordinator`, `restart-sentinel`, `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session-restart.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/update.test.ts` — all shards pass; `tsgo` core lane clean; core test-types lane has 0 non-`ui/` errors (the 2 `ui/app-sidebar.ts` errors reproduce identically on clean `main` with the diff stashed — pre-existing, unrelated).
- **Live A/B behavior proof** (real gateway, mock Telegram + mock LLM, real `gateway` tool call, config-watcher deferral winning the emission): after-fix run delivers exactly one sentinel recovery (`Gateway restart ok`) and exactly one continuation turn; before-fix run (`src/infra/restart.ts` reverted to `main`, rebuilt) loses both despite `continuationQueued: true`. Full logs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106174#issuecomment-4956370473
- Codex autoreview: clean, "patch is correct (0.88)", no actionable findings.

target.title: fix(agents): count CJK tool-result text by token-equivalent length
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The live per-turn tool-result truncation cap converts token budgets to character budgets with a flat 4-chars-per-token heuristic but measured tool-result text with raw UTF-16 `text.length`. A result made mostly of CJK text was accepted under the cap while its real token count was up to 4x the budget the cap exists to enforce.

**Solution**: Keep `toolResultMaxChars` as an independent **physical** UTF-16 ceiling and add a separate **token-equivalent** budget (the 30% context-share limit) measured with the existing CJK-aware `estimateStringChars` helper. The complete retained result must satisfy BOTH limits.

**What changed**: `getToolResultTextLength` stays a raw measurement (physical cap); a new `getToolResultEstimatedTextLength` measures token-equivalent length. `truncateToolResultText` gates on both budgets and re-checks the fully assembled prefix/tail/marker/suffix against the estimated budget, shrinking Unicode-safely. Plus tests and a docs note.

**What did NOT change**: The estimated budget is opt-in, so the persistence guard keeps its physical-only cap and pure ASCII behavior is byte-for-byte identical. The `maxChars` formula, the `toolResultMaxChars` config contract, and the output format are unchanged.

Fixes #103847

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `calculateMaxToolResultCharsWithCap` derives a token budget (`maxTokens * 4`) but the truncation compared/sliced against it using raw `text.length`. For CJK text (encoded at ~1 token/char, not ~1 token/4 chars) a 16000-char result reported 16000 against a 16000 cap and was never truncated, while its real cost was ~16000 tokens.

**Why This Change Was Made**: A maintainer's prior decision on this issue defined a two-budget contract — keep the configured cap as a physical UTF-16 ceiling and enforce a separate token-derived budget. This PR implements exactly that, reusing `estimateStringChars` (already used by `preemptive-compaction.ts`, `pruner.ts`, and `openai-transport-stream.ts`) rather than reinterpreting the physical config ceiling as a CJK-weighted one.

**User Impact**: CJK-heavy tool results are bounded to their real share of the context window without over-truncating results that already fit both budgets. ASCII/Latin content and the physical `toolResultMaxChars` ceiling are unaffected.

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: A tool result whose text is dense CJK (or other non-Latin) content whose raw UTF-16 length fits the physical cap but whose token-equivalent length exceeds the context-share budget.

**Root cause analysis**: The physical cap and the token budget were collapsed into one number and measured with raw `text.length`, so CJK content bypassed the token budget. A whole-input inflation ratio also cannot bound a compositionally different retained slice.

**Affected scope**: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.ts` — the live tool-result truncation path wired into `run.ts`, `run/attempt.ts`, and `session-tool-result-guard.ts`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Enforce a separate token-equivalent budget on the actual retained tool-result text while keeping `toolResultMaxChars` a physical UTF-16 ceiling.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64, Node.js 22.x, OpenClaw main @ 7ac8e2e227, real exported functions driven directly via `node --import tsx` (not mocked).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Drive the real exported functions with the mixed-script counterexample and the physical-cap / live-path cases:
```bash
node --import tsx -e "
import { truncateToolResultText, truncateOversizedToolResultsInMessages } from './src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.js';
import { estimateStringChars } from './src/utils/cjk-chars.js';
const mixed = '字'.repeat(5000) + 'a'.repeat(15000);
const r = truncateToolResultText(mixed, 1000000, { estimatedMaxChars: 16000 });
console.log('mixed retained est', estimateStringChars(r), '<=16000', estimateStringChars(r) <= 16000);
const cjk8k = [{ role: 'toolResult', content: [{ type: 'text', text: '字'.repeat(8000) }], id: 'a', timestamp: 1, toolCallId: 't' }];
console.log('8000 CJK truncatedCount', truncateOversizedToolResultsInMessages(cjk8k, 50000).truncatedCount);
"
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
== P1-2 mixed-script counterexample (old code emitted ~24142) ==
input estimated: 35000
retained estimated: 15781 | <= 16000: true

== P1-1 physical cap NOT CJK-weighted: 8000 CJK, physical 16000, ctx 50000 ==
truncatedCount: 0 (0 = not over-truncated)

== live path bounds large CJK to 30% token share ==
truncatedCount: 1 | retained est: 59781 | <= E(60000): true

== ASCII unchanged ==
8000 ASCII truncatedCount: 0 (0)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The mixed-script counterexample (CJK-heavy prefix + ASCII tail) retains 15781 estimated chars — within the 16000 budget — because the actual retained text is measured, not a whole-input average. An 8000-char CJK result that fits both budgets is not truncated (physical cap is not CJK-weighted). A 30000-char CJK result is bounded to 59781 estimated chars (the 30% share of a 50K context). ASCII is unchanged.

**What was not tested**: I did not run against a real provider tokenizer (no tokenizer library is bundled); the estimate uses the codebase's own `estimateStringChars`, already relied on in four sibling paths as the corrected estimate for this undercount class.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

```
pnpm test -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  73 passed (73)
   Duration  5.81s
```

Adds two-budget coverage: physical/estimated separation, the mixed-script overflow counterexample, CJK Extension B surrogate safety, and live-path integration (configured-cap no-op, large-CJK share bound, mixed-script, 50K/128K tiers). Related suites pass unchanged (`session-tool-result-guard` 35, `preemptive-compaction` 22). Also validated with `pnpm tsgo:core` (clean) and oxlint (clean).

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #103847
- **Related PRs**: #104055 (competing candidate for the same issue), #103901 (earlier attempt, closed after the two-budget design was defined)
- **In scope**: Per-result live truncation two-budget enforcement in `tool-result-truncation.ts`
- **Out of scope**: The separate aggregate tool-result budget (kept on its existing raw measurement)

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — ASCII behavior is byte-for-byte identical; the physical `toolResultMaxChars` ceiling is unchanged
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 73 tests pass, config contract unchanged

The start-screen ("New session") target row chips — agent, workspace folder, and gateway/device — rendered their Lucide icons as solid black blobs. `ui/src/styles/new-session.css` sized the SVGs but never set `stroke: currentColor; fill: none`, so the path-only icon templates fell back to the SVG default (black fill, no stroke). In dark mode the icons were nearly invisible; in light mode they read as filled blobs instead of the outline icon style used everywhere else in the Control UI.

target.title: fix(memory-core): clear pending-update wait timer after update settles
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `memory_search` calls during an in-flight QMD reindex would each leak a ref'd 500ms timer. `QmdMemoryManager.waitForPendingUpdateBeforeSearch` races the pending reindex update against a `setTimeout`-based 500ms bound; when the pending update resolved first (the common case - reindex completes in under 500ms), the timeout was never cleared, so each search left a pending timer. Sustained `memory_search` traffic during a reindex stacked pending timers, each holding event-loop interest until it fired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The wait helper now captures the `setTimeout` handle and clears it in a `finally` when the pending update settles first, following the same `try/finally + clearTimeout` convention already used by the sibling memory-core wait helpers (`manager-embedding-ops.ts`, `tools.ts`) and by `packages/ai/src/internal/retry-sleep.ts`, whose comment documents the identical leak class: "Successful retry waits must detach from the run-level signal; otherwise every retry retains this promise closure until the whole run aborts." The method's contract is unchanged - it still waits up to 500ms for a pending update to settle before proceeding - and the change is bounded to the one leaf method. No new helper is introduced; the inline `try/finally + clearTimeout` matches the local convention.

## User Impact

**Before:** each `memory_search` during an active reindex left a pending 500ms timer when the reindex finished quickly, and repeated searches stacked them.

**After:** the wait timer is cleared as soon as the pending update settles. The fast path (search proceeds immediately) and the full-500ms-wait path are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Stock pinned main (`08843c74de`) retained 50 pending `Timeout` handles after 50 production wait calls where the pending update resolved first; each was the 500ms wait timeout, left pending because the operation arm won the race without clearing it.
- Current-head production timer-lifecycle proof used the real `QmdMemoryManager.waitForPendingUpdateBeforeSearch()` method with real Node timers and `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()`:

  ```text
  BEFORE 08843c74de (origin/main)
  iterations=50
  pendingResolvedQuickly=true
  baselineTimeouts=0
  afterTimeouts=50
  leakedTimeouts=50

  AFTER fix
  iterations=50
  pendingResolvedQuickly=true
  baselineTimeouts=0
  afterTimeouts=0
  leakedTimeouts=0
  ```

  The uncommitted harness imported the real `QmdMemoryManager` class, created a real instance carrying the real prototype method (the method reads only `this.pendingUpdate`; the full `create()` factory spawns the external qmd process, which is out of scope for this timer-lifecycle proof), set `pendingUpdate` to an already-resolved `Promise` (reindex completed in under 500ms, the common case), and counted actual pending `Timeout` handles via Node's `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()`. Both runs were reproducible across two executions each.
- Committed regression guard (`qmd-manager.timer-leak.test.ts`): 1 file passed, 1 test passed. Uses real timers and `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` (no fake timers, no mock assertions); verified to fail on the base (positive delta) and pass on the fix.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.test.ts` -> 8 failed | 141 passed on base; 8 failed | 145 passed on fix. The 8 failures are pre-existing SQLite store-writer-queue failures, identical on `origin/main` and unrelated to this timer change; zero new failures introduced.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.timer-leak.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.timer-leak.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`

Impact-surface review traced `pendingUpdate` from its set site (`this.pendingUpdate = run().finally(() => { this.pendingUpdate = null; })`) through `waitForPendingUpdateBeforeSearch` and its single caller in `search()`, and checked sibling memory-core wait helpers (all already clear their timers on settle). A fresh open-PR search found no PR covering this timer leak.

Fix classification: root cause fix. No schema, default, migration, protocol, or provider behavior changes.

target.title: fix(config): restore env changes before rethrowing INVALID_CONFIG
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadConfigLocal()` applies `env.vars` to `process.env` during config resolution via `resolveConfigForRead()` → `applyConfigEnvVars()`. When config validation fails with `INVALID_CONFIG`, the catch block at line 1942 rethrows without restoring the env snapshot, leaking env side effects into the running process.

**Trigger**: An `openclaw.json` with valid `env.vars` entries but other invalid config sections. Running `openclaw doctor` on such a config would leave `process.env` polluted with the vars from the invalid config.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three other code paths in the same file already follow the correct pattern of calling `restoreEnvChangesIfUnchanged()` before returning/retrying after config operations that modify env:

| Location | Scenario |
|---|---|
| Line 1906 | `loadConfigLocal()` — retry after suspicious recovery |
| Line 2169 | `readConfigFileSnapshotInternal()` — retry after suspicious recovery |
| Line 3242 | `writeAndActivateConfig()` — rollback after write failure |

The `INVALID_CONFIG` path was the only one missing this cleanup.

## User Impact

- Before: invalid config with `env.vars` → env leaked → subsequent operations see wrong env values
- After: env is properly restored before rethrowing, matching the behavior of all other error/retry paths

## Evidence

- Static analysis: `grep -n restoreEnvChangesIfUnchanged src/config/io.ts` confirms 3 existing call sites at lines 1906, 2169, 3242, all following the same snapshot-before / snapshot-after / restore pattern around lines 1778-1909
- `restoreEnvChangesIfUnchanged()` (line 1403) is safe/stable: only restores keys where `env[key] === after[key]`, meaning it won't clobber external env mutations

target.title: feat(mobile): default pairing to full node access
target.body:
Closes #105843

## What Problem This Solves

The official iOS and Android apps connected as nodes, but mobile QR/setup-code pairing only handed them a bounded operator credential. Users therefore missed normal full node/operator behavior unless they manually approved more access, and native settings did not explain the limited state or upgrade path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Official mobile pairing now issues the node credential plus full operator access by default. Full access is restricted to the exact official mobile bootstrap profile and matching native client metadata; arbitrary bootstrap profiles remain bounded. Control UI and `openclaw qr --limited` preserve an explicit limited-access fallback, and rescanning a Full access code upgrades an existing limited mobile pairing.

## User Impact

iOS and Android pair as fully usable nodes by default. Operators who prefer least privilege can choose Limited access, while both native settings screens show Full/Limited state and tell limited users to rescan a Full access QR code to upgrade.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxckgwbgms3d3n72gc5kpkky` (`violet-barnacle-a620`): `pnpm check:changed` passed all selected core, core-test, UI, extension, app, and docs lanes in 14m07s.
- Gateway authorization suites: 82/82 passed; includes full handoff, bounded limited credential verification, and same-identity limited-to-full upgrade.
- CLI setup: 24/24 passed; black-box default/`--limited` exercise reported Full/Limited respectively, issued non-empty distinct setup codes, and exposed no credential values.
- Control UI Chromium E2E passed; recorded request sequence `full -> limited -> full -> full`, proving regeneration and reset-on-reopen. Before/after artifacts retained in the Testbox run.
- Android: `pnpm android:lint` and `pnpm android:test` passed (34 Gradle tasks). Native i18n generation/check, protocol/Swift generation checks, and targeted SwiftFormat passed.

target.title: docs: fix pnpm global install build approval
target.body:
Closes #106166

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users following the pnpm global install instructions would hit `[ERR_PNPM_APPROVE_BUILDS_NOT_SUPPORTED_WITH_GLOBAL]` when running `pnpm approve-builds -g`. Because that command fails, the required build step could remain unapproved.

## Why This Change Was Made

pnpm no longer supports `approve-builds -g` for isolated global packages. The install command now uses pnpm's supported `--allow-build=openclaw` option, while local source-checkout instructions that use `pnpm approve-builds` without `-g` remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Users can follow the pnpm global install instructions without encountering the unsupported-command error, including through the localized install pages generated from this source.

## Evidence

- pnpm's current `approve-builds` documentation explicitly directs global installs to use `--allow-build`.
- The `pnpm add` reference documents `--allow-build` for authorizing install scripts.
- The final diff changes only `docs/install/index.md` and passes `git show --check`.
- Local docs formatting could not run because this isolated checkout does not have the `oxfmt` dependency installed; CI remains the format gate.

Users could not start provider-native sessions from a session catalog header, and a Claude Code session created through OpenClaw could appear twice: once under Claude Code and again under the owning agent's Chats group.

The backing OpenClaw session remains intact for execution; only its duplicate sidebar presentation is removed.

Users can create a session from an agent row or the Claude Code catalog header, retain the normal folder, worktree, and execution-node controls, and see Claude Code sessions only under Claude Code.

## What Problem This Solves

Quarantined skill workshop proposals were a dead end: users could not see scan findings, could not restore them to pending, and had no path forward in the UI. The only workaround was manually editing `proposal.json`.

Fixes #106134

Three concrete problems addressed:

1. **Scan findings invisible**: `SkillWorkshopProposal` type dropped `scan` and `statusReason` fields. Now they're displayed in the UI for quarantined proposals.
2. **No restore action**: Backend `withPendingSkillProposalMutation` gates all mutations on `status === "pending"`, so quarantined proposals had zero available operations.
3. **No restore button**: UI only rendered action buttons for pending proposals.

## User Impact

- Quarantined proposals now show scan findings (severity badges, file:line, rule message) in the detail card
- New "Restore" button moves quarantined proposals back to pending state
- Restore re-scans content for fresh security assessment (consistent with apply behavior)
- Restored proposals can then be revised and re-applied

target.title: fix(tasks): reconcile CLI subagent cancellation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This is a narrow cancellation-path follow-up for TaskFlow rows that already have a tracked child relationship but do not get fully reconciled today.

In local upgrade-replay incidents, operator cancellation could fail to clear active task state or could clear only the registry row while leaving a backing child session alive:

- stale subagent wrapper rows could return `Subagent was not running.` and stay non-terminal, blocking flow cancellation with `One or more child tasks are still active.`
- `runtime=cli` task rows whose `childSessionKey` points at a `:subagent:` child could be marked cancelled without killing the backing child session, allowing the child to continue appending events or reappear after restart

This PR keeps the fix at the operator cancellation entrypoint. It does not replace #90505, which is a broader maintenance-side reconciliation fix for killed subagent task rows and carries a separate session-state transition/docs tradeoff.

## Summary

- cancel CLI-tracked tasks with `childSessionKey` pointing at a `:subagent:` child by killing the backing subagent session before marking the registry row cancelled
- preserve backing subagent terminal/finalizing outcomes before cancelling CLI mirror rows, so a late `succeeded`/`failed`/finalizing state is not overwritten by operator cancellation
- keep direct/main CLI follow-up rows registry-only so cancelling them does not kill the user's main session
- allow found-but-not-running subagent wrappers to fall through to registry cancellation instead of returning `Subagent was not running.`
- keep childless ACP `context_engine_turn_maintenance` rows non-cancellable without an owner handoff, because active deferred maintenance rows need an owner-aware cancellation path

## Relationship to existing work

Related issue: #90444.

This is a narrow follow-up to the uncovered operator-facing cancellation cases described in #90444. It intentionally does not change the broader maintenance reconciliation model covered by #90505.

#90505 remains the larger active/candidate fix for killed subagent task-row finalization. This PR only addresses cancellation entrypoints that can otherwise leave TaskFlow rows or backing child sessions inconsistent even when an operator explicitly tries to repair the state with `tasks cancel` / `tasks flow cancel`.

## Evidence

Local production/operator evidence, sanitized:

- `openclaw tasks cancel` returned `Subagent was not running.` for a found-but-stopped subagent wrapper, but the task row stayed non-terminal and continued blocking flow cancellation.
- A `runtime=cli` task with a `:subagent:` child session was marked cancelled in the task registry without stopping the backing child session; after restart/restore, the child could continue producing events and the task could effectively reappear as running.
- After applying the CLI/subagent cancellation-path behavior locally, restarting the gateway, and replaying the affected cleanup, `running=0`, `queued=0`, and task audit no longer reported stale running/queued/cancel-stuck rows for these cases.

Focused validation on this branch:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.test.ts`
  - `src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts`: `Tests 113 passed (113)`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.test.ts`: `Tests 21 passed (21)`
- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/tasks/task-registry.ts src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.test.ts`

## Negative Boundaries

- Does not change the `lost -> succeeded` maintenance reconciliation rule discussed in #90505.
- Does not attempt to solve the larger session write-lock / session-state design line.
- Does not kill direct/main CLI child sessions; those remain registry-only cancellation to avoid terminating the user's main conversation.
- Does not overwrite backing subagent terminal/finalizing outcomes when a CLI mirror row cancellation races with completion.
- Does not mark childless `acp/context_engine_turn_maintenance` rows cancelled without an owner-aware cancellation handoff; stale maintenance cleanup should be handled by a separate owner-aware follow-up.
